quote: We now propose that the expansion of the Universe can act as a mechanism that selects the decoupling frame

quote: One obvious possibility is that these excitations were produced copiously in the early universe and they are still around as dark matter.

quote: Universality of gravity also suggests that all quantum fields, including those in the SM, should have extended non-local excitations of the type discussed here, in addition to the standard particle-like excitations.

quote: However, since SM excitations are all charged, their presence, with the exception of the neutrino, would probably be detectable via coherent interactions with photons or some other SM quanta.
reading: In 2016 the charged partners are said to be visible and to have decayed early. This differs from the 2019-2020 'dual Standard Model as the dark sector' (my reading).

quote: Some weakly interacting chargeless non-local quanta would be the perfect candidates for dark matter. These could be the non-local versions of neutrinos, or some non-SM fields yet to be detected. Their non-locality would explain their invisibility to dark-matter detection experiments which rely on localized interactions between localized quanta.
reading: Non-locality is offered as the explanation of null direct detection, a related idea to C3, but here the quanta are extended rather than localized in momentum.

quote: Due to their extended nature in both space and momentum, once created, it may be difficult for such excitations to decay into local ones which are localized in either space or momentum.
reading: The quanta are extended in both space and momentum, the opposite of #11 §12's monopoles localized in momentum.

quote: Their extended nature could also render them sensitive to global aspects of spacetime, such as the Hubble parameter, and may explain Milgram scaling observed in spiral galaxies
reading: The modified-dark-matter acceleration scale.

quote: We note that these points are also implied by the framework of metastring theory
reading: Links the idea to the metastring.

quote: We expect that such non-local excitations (as part of a covariant non-commutative formulation, as implied by the metastring [131, 132]) can serve as unusual dark matter quanta.
reading: Metastring non-local excitations proposed as dark-matter quanta, September 2017.

quote: Roughly, the zero mode sector looks like two entangled particles, and it could be viewed as a model for modified dark matter quanta discussed in this review
where: conclusion (footnote 13: metaparticle theory 'currently being developed by' Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman, Leigh and Minic)
reading: The claim of Minic 2020's abstract, metaparticle quanta as dark matter, already in writing 29.5 months before it (899 days, computed).

quote: How strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter? How does MDM self-interact?

quote: If the quanta of MDM indeed obey infinite statistics, as suggested in Ref. [103], it is possible that there are (dark) stars made of such quanta.

quote: Thus, MDM quanta are not particle-like, but might be modeled as metaparticles, excitations of metastrings, which look roughly like two entangled particles in momentum space.

reading: 'Duality' here is between cold dark matter and MOND, two readings of an entropic force. There is no dual sector: full-text search finds no 'T-dual' and no 'string'.

quote: For concreteness, let us start with a vector background, by shifting the momenta and the dual momenta by the standard, minimally coupled gauge field and its dual [14]:
reading: Dual fields enter as background fields of the dual momentum: p → p + A(x,x̃), p̃ → p̃ + Ã(x,x̃). A dark field is the gauge field that couples to p̃, the momentum of x̃. It is not matter localized in the momentum of x (my reading).

quote: In other words, in the observable spacetime, the visible sector and its dual/dark counterpart are “mixed/correlated” (19), in a way that is sensitive to both the UV and IR cutoffs. quote: scaling coefficient in (21), forced on dimensional grounds in this mass-mixing term, sets the scale in this novel “seesaw mechanism,” in principle tunable to induce naturally small neutrino masses.

reading: Every fermion–dual-fermion pair has a mass matrix [[m, λ⁹/L¹⁰],[λ⁹/L¹⁰, m̃]]. This is a proposal ('may well').

quote: We note that, quite explicitly, the dark matter sector provides “sources” for the visible matter sector.
reading: Through λ⁸/L¹⁰⟦φ,φ̃⟧, which the paper calls 'an explicit correlation between the dark matter sector and a visible sector'.

quote: In the dual QED sector, we should find a dual photon that is correlated to the visible photon, and that is distinct from the dark photon of effective field theory. reading: Stated with a citation to MDM [12]. 'Correlated' with visible matter is part of the claim from the start.

reading: The paper sets Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹ (T-duality), which yields Tseytlin's intensive action. A structural parallel to #11 §10's a·ã = 1 (App. A item 6), my comparison.

reading: Points to a dynamical dark energy ([51]: Jejjala, Kavic, Minic 2007; Jejjala, Kavic, Minic, Takeuchi arXiv:2011.08852). No w is given here.

quote: The above metaparticle-like dark matter quanta are by construction correlated to visible matter and have been discussed in the literature as Modified dark matter (MDM).
reading: The correlation is built in ('by construction'), and the dark quanta are identified with MDM.

quote: This “fundamental acceleration” is just the value of \Lambda expressed as acceleration \sim cH_{0} , where H_{0} is the Hubble constant
reading: An acceleration scale cH₀ of order 10⁻¹⁰ m/s², said to appear in galactic and cluster fits and in the baryonic Tully–Fisher (BTF) and baryonic Faber–Jackson (BFJ) relations. The program predicts a knee in σ_T(v) instead (#11 §13 row 1).

reading: Takes dark matter collisionless, for the analogy. #11 §8's χ has a velocity-gated self-interaction.

reading: A stated prediction, from dimensional analysis: about 10⁻¹⁰ m/s² for clusters, 10⁻⁹ for galaxies, 10⁻⁸ for globular clusters (their Fig. 1).
correction: The paper calls it 'One intriguing prediction of the above discussion is the possible z-dependence' and its basis 'this simple handwaving argument' (both FOUND); 'a stated prediction' is stronger than the text.

quote: In this paper, we propose that the BFJ relation could be explained by metaparticle-based, or similar MDM models. We are, however, mindful that it could well be explained by more conventional means.
reading: The authors' own caveat. They add that 'MDM models, though suggestive, are lacking in similar concrete scenarios that would connect the models to the BFJ relation'.

quote: In particular, the modular representation of QFT introduces dual “electric” and “magnetic” variables, which are non-commuting in general.
reading: Electric and magnetic variables in the modular representation; no monopoles or magnetically charged matter.

reading: The other choice of half is the mirror, an equally valid description. Bears on #11 P5's 'the mirror vacuum is equally lawful' (my reading). No selection mechanism.

reading: η pairs the roots of the E8 built on x with those of the Ẽ8 built on x̃, which the authors read as the Langlands (electric–magnetic, GNO) duality of gauge groups. This is the closest point in my papers to #11 §11.3–§11.4. It names no magnetic charges and no monopoles.

reading: Each gauge field on x has a 'dark' dual on x̃ in the same algebra: A^α(x), A^α̃(x) and their duals Ã^α(x̃), Ã^α̃(x̃).

reading: A correlation term (λ₄²/L⁴)∫𝔉^{μν}⟦A^α_μ(x), Ã^β̃_ν(x̃)⟧η_{αβ̃} couples the visible E8 fields to the dark fields of the Langlands-dual factor. It is called 'a straightforward but novel result [21]', [21] being 2010.15610.

quote: in addition to an exponentially suppressed positive cosmological constant.
reading: A positive cosmological constant (w = −1) on a de Sitter bubble-world in a stringy cosmic-brane construction. It is not a dual-spacetime mechanism.

quote: the accelerated expansion of our universe implies an asymptotically and approximately de Sitter (dS) geometry with a small but positive cosmological constant
reading: The paper takes the observed acceleration as de Sitter with a positive constant. It does not consider w ≠ −1.

quote: the axilaton models can be made dynamical by choosing their anisotropy, \omega , differently on the two sides of the candidate for the observed universe,
reading: 'Two sides' means the two regions of the transverse space around the brane-world, as in AdS-bubble nucleation. They are not a dual or conjugate universe, so nothing here bears on C5 (my reading).

reading: A candidacy. It cites [254], Freidel–Leigh–Minic 2019 (IJMPA 34, 1941004, not on arXiv), and [255], Minic 2020; the correlation is cited to MDM.

reading: Dual gravity R̃(x̃) yields our cosmological constant. #11 §7's momentum gravity is a massive spin-2 X instead.

quote: We see that although p,{\mathord{\tilde{p}\mkern 1.0mu}} might resemble a doubling of momentum space, the propagator contains a simple pole along with a \delta -function constraint.
reading: p and p̃ are two separate momenta. The usual spectrum is the singular limit μ = 0, p̃ = 0.

quote: is effectively spontaneously broken. Here the novel feature is that the internal symmetry is non-compact
reading: The only spontaneous breaking in these papers: the second Lorentz group O(1,d−1)₂, inside a sector of fixed non-zero p̃. It is not a breaking of Born duality or a choice of polarization. Compare #11 §3, P2′.
correction: Not the only spontaneous breaking in these papers: 2212.06086 §2.2 reviews KKLT and LVS, which 'break supersymmetry spontaneously' (FOUND). The point that matters stands: no paper breaks Born duality or the polarization spontaneously.

quote: Although we will not consider metaparticle interactions directly in this paper, such interactions preserve both p and
reading: Interactions conserve p and p̃ separately. There is no momentum-overlap gate (compare #11 §8).

reading: A static potential e^{−αr}/r^β cos(γr), with α, β, γ functions of m, μ, d (cited as unpublished work of Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman, Leigh and Minic). It has no dependence on relative velocity.

reading: The μ ≠ 0 metaparticle extension is proposed for dark-matter phenomenology; μ = 0 is the sector of ordinary particles.

quote: Thus the usual detection analysis of particulate dark matter should be revisited in the context of metaparticle kinematics and representation theory.
reading: Calls for a revised detection analysis. It states no expected null.

quote: that in the early (small) universe the dual (“dark”) degrees of freedom dominate, and that in the old (large) universe the visible degrees of freedom are dominant.

quote: This fundamental, primordial length-scale, \lambda , should not be confused with the 3{+}1 -dimensional Planck length
reading: In the axilaton models, λ ∼ (M_P^(10))⁻¹ ≲ 10⁻¹⁹ m. My computation: ħc/λ for λ = 1e-19 m is 1.97 TeV.

reading: The dual volume sets Newton's constant, a possible route to the H0 tension. Compare #11 §10's 'a⁻⁶ step in G_eff'.

quote: In this subsection we discuss the dual matter degrees of freedom and the explicit appearance of dark matter in the general formulation of string theory[242].
reading: Cites [242], Freidel–Leigh–Minic PLB 730 (2014) (arXiv:1307.7080). Its full text has no 'dark matter' (my search), so the citation is to the formalism.

quote: plus a characteristic coupling inherited from the symplectic structure (which is clearly not present in the usual effective field theory approach)

Its meaning: a dark field does not commute with its visible field, by analogy with p and q, an induced Heisenberg algebra in field space. #11 P4 has χ as a separate p-polarized species coupled by gravity alone. Same word, different relation (my reading).

quote: Note the relevance of the very light dual degrees of freedom in the observed spacetime in connection with the H_{0} tension, which could be resolved by changing the effective number of light dark matter degrees of freedom — dark radiation.
reading: Light dual degrees of freedom as dark radiation, suggested as helping with H0. #11 §11.4 treats a p-sector photon as dark radiation bounded by ξ < 0.760 (round-3 ruling 5).

reading: In 4d the vector mixing is −(λ₄²/L⁴)𝓕^{ab}⟦A_a,Ã_b⟧, with dimensionless 'Berry phase-like background fluxes' 𝓕. The authors call the sectors 'coupled'.

quote: different cosmological scenarios result in differing estimates for both \lambda_{4} and L , so here we leave them unspecified.

reading: Scalars too, through (λ₄²/L⁴)𝔉⟦φ,φ̃⟧. Axions likewise (eq. 6.34).

reading: The fermion mixing (λ₄³/L⁴)𝔉(⟦ψ̄,ψ̃⟧ + h.c.).

quote: the dual matter degrees of freedom naturally appear as dark matter degrees of freedom, as discussed in the preceding section.

reading: From (λ₄²/L⁴)⟦φ,φ̃⟧. The dark sector 'provides “sources”' for the visible one.

reading: A dual neutrino.

quote: may well be phenomenologically relevant — even for a minuscule numerical value of
reading: Eq. (6.36): the mixing shifts the masses by δm = λ₄⁶/(L⁸(m − m̃)), and the gap 2δm may matter when m ≈ m̃. The paper adds: 'This clearly involves model-dependent details, and must be left to a case-by-case analysis.'

reading: As in 2010.15610 §5. A dual Z is distinguished from a Z′ by its correlation with the visible Z.

reading: The list that follows reads [q,q̃] = il_P², [q,p] = i, [q̃,p̃] = i, [p,p̃] = 0. The dual has its own momentum.

quote: In our approach the CP violating phases would come from the SM calculation and the dual SM sector as well from the intrinsic CP violation of quantum gravity in the non-perturbative metastring theory.
reading: The dual SM is taken to feed visible CP violation: another non-gravitational tie.

quote: The invisible (dark) sector is spanned by the dual fields \tilde{\phi}(x,\tilde{x}) , which may well be subject to a third quantization indeterminacy because of an induced non-commutativity between visible \phi and dual (invisible/dark) \tilde{\phi} fields.

reading: Dark energy is a cosmological constant (w = −1).

reading: The essay's only mention of metaparticles, as context. It has no dark-matter statement: 'dark' occurs 0 times in the full text (executed grep). It also has no dual coordinate x̃ and no polarization.

quote: Born geometry requires two distinct sets of coordinates to describe, x and \tilde{x} . In such a scenario, one can establish that commutators of local operators e.g. [x,y] commute, preserving our familiar spacetime causality, but commutators of the form [x,\tilde{x}] do not, which allows for a violation of factorizability and a modification of the Born rule.

reading: x̃ is a second set of coordinates of Born geometry, and [x, x̃] ≠ 0 is what lets the Born rule be modified without breaking spacetime causality. This passage gives x̃ no scale and does not say whether it is a momentum or a winding coordinate.

quote: in which apart from spacetime coordinates x one has dual spacetime coordinates \tilde{x} which do not commute with x . The pair x and \tilde{x} is put together into a doublet \mathbb{X} .

reading: In the metastring matrix model, x̃ are 'dual spacetime coordinates' that do not commute with x and are paired with x in the doublet 𝕏. No dark sector appears. §7 uses the vacuum-energy see-saw l_λ ~ √(l l_P), which the record already treats as prior art (phase-space-diameter note), to put the triple-interference scale near the Higgs scale.

quote: Here we note that modular spacetime is a notion of quantum spacetime, corresponding to a generic polarization of quantum theory [11]. Note that in the context of modular spacetime, x^{\mu} are the usual spacetime coordinates, while p_{\nu} are dual coordinates conjugate to x .
reading: In modular spacetime the 'dual coordinates conjugate to x' are the momenta p, with the canonical [x̂, p̂] = i (ℏ = 1). That is the single phase space of #11 (P1, P2′). 'Polarization' here means the modular (Zak) representation, called generic; it is not a choice between x and p.
correction: The paper never mentions the Zak transform ('Zak' has 0 matches in 2305.12593). It defines modular spacetime as 'the space of all commuting subalgebras of the above Heisenberg algebra, which is equivalent to a discrete self-dual lattice in phase space'. The Zak gloss comes from another paper, 2407.06207 §3.3 ('modular polarization (defined via the Zak transform)'). The rest of the reading stands.

quote: In the limit of large expansion a\to\infty , the dual dimension shrinks to zero and one recovers the usual spacetime.
reading: The preceding sentence rescales x → ax, p → a⁻¹p, which keeps the commutator. This is the kinematics of #11 §10's a·ã = 1 (App. A item 6), used here as a limit that recovers classical spacetime, not as an evolution in time. The record's C5 finding for this paper reads it the same way.
correction: Here a rescales the modular cell (x → ax, p → a⁻¹p). It is not a cosmological scale factor. So the passage is a kinematic analogue of #11 §10's a·ã = 1, which is the wording of the record's C5 finding, not 'the kinematics of' it. The rest is right, including 'not as an evolution in time'.

quote: As already stated, in the context of metastring theory apart from the usual spacetime coordinates x^{\mu} one also encounters \tilde{x}_{\nu} , dual coordinates conjugate to x . These coordinates are the eigenvalues of operators which do not commute (in addition to the usual canonical commutators between coordinates and dual momenta),
reading: The same words, 'dual coordinates conjugate to x', now name x̃ in the metastring. x̃ fails to commute with x 'in addition to' the canonical commutators with the 'dual momenta', so here x̃ is a further coordinate beside p, not p itself.

quote: [\hat{x}^{\mu},\hat{\tilde{x}}_{\nu}]=i\pi\lambda^{2}\delta^{\mu}_{\nu}\hat{I}. This commutation relation can be deduced through a careful analysis of the zero mode sector of string theory where \lambda^{2}=\hbar\alpha^{\prime} [18], but in general, the scale \lambda depends on the context.
reading: The scale is λ² = ħα′ from the string zero modes, but λ 'depends on the context'. The factor π is this paper's normalization; the other papers give iλ², 2πiλ² and 2πiℓ_s².

quote: This is the decoupling limit where a modular field \phi(x,\tilde{x}) is restricted to the usual notion of a spacetime field \phi(x) (for example, a SM field), as considered in the context of EFT. In this limit metaparticles (correlated objects of visible particles and their duals, which, in turn, represent natural candidates for dark matter [10]) are reduced to canonical particles.
reading: The paper's only statement of the identification: a parenthesis, proposed ('natural candidates'), citing [10]. [10] is BHM arXiv:2212.06086, plus arXiv:2111.14205, LHEP 2021 and two 2019 papers. Grammatically the antecedent of 'which' may be either the duals or the metaparticles (my reading). The 'decoupling limit' is a limit of the dual cell's size (b → ∞), not an energy scale; in it the dual sector drops out of the effective field theory.
correction: The reader reads the parenthesis, its hedging and its citation [10] correctly. 'In it the dual sector drops out of the effective field theory' is the reader's inference. The text says only that the modular field is restricted to a spacetime field and that metaparticles 'are reduced to canonical particles'; it does not say what becomes of the dark-matter candidates. The inference also conflicts with 2407.06207 §3.4, where integrating over x̃ leaves the dark matter in the effective theory: 'In the above expression one needs to integrate over the dual space coordinates x̃ to get an effective description of visible matter, A(x), and dark matter, Ã(x), in classical x spacetime'.

quote: Also, in the limit of large expansion b\to\infty , the dual spacetime dimension shrinks to zero and one recovers the usual spacetime notions.
reading: The same rescaling, now applied to (x, x̃) through x → bx, x̃ → b⁻¹x̃. It is the limit in which the dark (dual) sector disappears from the effective theory.
correction: The rescaling x → bx, x̃ → b⁻¹x̃ is read correctly. 'It is the limit in which the dark (dual) sector disappears from the effective theory' is the reader's inference, not the paper's statement (see the correction to the previous item).

The verifier derived the brackets from the paper's own Lagrangian, L_mp = p·ẋ + p̃·(dx̃/dτ) + λ² p·(dp̃/dτ), and got {x, x̃} = λ², {x, p} = {x̃, p̃} = 1, {p, p̃} = 0, rank 4 (brackets_v.out). The dark fields need the doubled algebra, since they are backgrounds of p̃, but the paper does not separate the two uses of x̃: it identifies them.

quote: Different observers see different spacetimes (slices of modular spacetime). However, different spacetimes are in linear superposition, and so fundamental length/time is consistent with the Lorentz symmetry.

quote: (We will argue that dual particles, correlated to visible particles, represent dark matter.) If we turn on backgrounds p\to p+\phi and \tilde{p}\to\tilde{p}+\tilde{\phi} . quote: However, the visible \phi and invisible (dark matter) {\tilde{\phi}} do not commute. Therefore, one could say that dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime.

correction: The passage states that φ and φ̃ do not commute and that dark matter is therefore 'fuzzy'. It does not say that this non-commutation is what 'correlated' means. Equating the two is the reader's inference, presented as the paper's statement ('The correlation is stated as non-commutativity').

reading: Cites FKGLM 2021. The wording is close to #11 App. A item 2 ('one state, two descriptions'), but no dynamics are given (my comparison).

The prediction dates from July 2014, not from the paper's first-posted date.

quote: Whether such a dark matter profile can be realized dynamically will depend on the detailed nature of the MDM quanta and their interactions with ordinary matter.
reading: Central to Q4: the profile is a phenomenological input. How it arises dynamically, including any interaction with ordinary matter, is left to the unknown nature of the quanta.
correction: The next sentence qualifies 'left to the unknown nature of the quanta': 'We have presented several ideas on how this may be arranged in previous publications' [31, 32, 33] (FOUND). Those are the Ho–Minic–Ng papers on infinite statistics and the Born–Infeld analogy. No interaction term is given.

quote: Our approach differs from these papers in the crucial fact that it assumes an actual source of dark matter, which, however, is not of a traditional particle type (i.e. it is not described by a local effective quantum field theory).
reading: MDM is a real dark-matter source but not a local particle. This is the property the authors rely on; no coupling is specified.
correction: This sentence was added in v2 (15 Jul 2014). v1 (14 Aug 2013) has only a conditional: 'If MDM quanta obey infinite statistics (in some sense a middle quantum statistics between the usual Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics), they should not be described by a local quantum field theory of particles.' (v1 PDF, FOUND loose; FOUND in v2).

quote: In the CDM paradigm, accelerations are determined by General Relativity and the addition of massive particles that interact only gravitationally, dark matter.
reading: Their CDM is gravity-only. MDM is set apart from it by Λ ('In MDM, the critical acceleration is introduced through the cosmological constant', same paragraph, code-checked FOUND) and by the nature of the quanta, not by a stated non-gravitational interaction.
correction: This sentence and the paragraph contrasting CDM, MOND and MDM were added in v2 (15 Jul 2014); they are not in v1 (14 Aug 2013). The reading stands for v2.

quote: in the hopes that the model's predictions can be checked against data from experiments such as Fermi-LAT
reading: Indirect detection: a hope that gamma-ray maps could test the predicted profile; footnote 4 adds that such signals could be astrophysical (pulsars). The paper does not say what would produce the gamma rays (my observation).

quote: Besides obeying different statistics, MDM has some unusual inertial properties (see Equation (A9)). This provides a natural explanation for the measured underdensity of dark matter in the solar system
reading: The paper continues that the External Field Effect 'is built into the inertial properties of MDM, so we do not expect to see dark matter effects in the Solar system' (code-checked FOUND), and notes Bovy & Tremaine's contrary, standard density. My inference: a lower local density would lower direct-detection rates; the paper does not draw this.

quote: so the dark matter must track the baryonic matter
reading: M′ ∝ M, so the dark matter tracks the baryons by construction of the profile. The paper adds that M′ depends on a_c, read as 'the dark matter being knowledgable about the Hubble parameter'.

quote: Despite its appearance, Eq. (18) does not modify General Relativity (GR) since the derivation of the right-hand-side is based on GR.
reading: Einstein's equations are unchanged. The MDM relation is a_N[1 + f_MDM(a/a0)] = √(a² + a0²) − a0, with a0 = c²√(Λ/3) = cH0 = 2πa_c (Eq. 20). By code, cH0 = 6.58×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² for H0 = 67.74 km/s/Mpc (paper: (6.581 ± 0.045)×10⁻⁸ cm/s²).

quote: is conveyed to the dark-matter via the temperature of the de Sitter horizon
reading: The channel by which the dark matter 'knows' Λ is the de Sitter horizon temperature: a thermodynamic statement, not a force between dark matter and baryons.

quote: This choice is, of course, arbitrary and a case of reverse engineering.
reading: The authors' own word for the 2010–2014 profile f_MDM = (1/π)(a0/a)². Section 2 then motivates (1/2)(a0/a)² by a Jacobson-type thermodynamic argument. They add 'Despite lacking a dynamical theory, which precludes performing numerical simulations,' (code-checked FOUND).

quote: Thus the energy momentum tensor of the extra sources (which we will identify with missing mass) has to be related to the energy momentum tensor of ordinary visible matter
reading: The relation is between stress tensors, T′_αβ = (a0²/2a²)T_αβ (Eq. 36) and M′ = (a0²/2a²)M (Eq. 37): a proportionality fixed by temperatures, with no interaction term. My reading of Eq. 37: a0² = c⁴Λ/3, so M′ ∝ Λ at fixed a.

quote: Our dark matter mass profile thus “knows” about the visible matter as well as the cosmological background
reading: The paper's own phrasing of the tie: the profile 'knows' about visible matter, about the background and about inertia. The section closes 'From our perspective, flat galactic rotation curves are a quantum gravity effect at large scales.' (code-checked FOUND).

quote: We have shown that MDM performs as well as CDM, and considerably better than MOND (which only works well at the galactic scale), for all clusters in our sample.
reading: Data: 13 low-redshift relaxed clusters of Vikhlinin et al. 2006 (Chandra, with ROSAT-PSPC where deep enough; 0.7–9 keV; hydrostatic masses). The authors assign a 1σ error of 10%. The generalized profile f = α/[1 + r/r_MDM](a0/a)² fits with α ∼ 100 and r_MDM ∼ 10 kpc, and galaxies are refit with α = 0.5 and r_MDM = 20 kpc. MOND fails in both magnitude and shape.

quote: needs to change by two orders of magnitude. This is not completely unrealistic, given our heuristic thermodynamic reasoning, but we have to admit of being ignorant of the underlying reason for this.
reading: Against-evidence stated by the authors: α must change by two orders of magnitude (∼1 to ∼100; log10 = 2.0 by code) between galaxies and clusters, for no known reason.

quote: A more concrete theory for MDM quanta will allow us to test this idea at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments.
reading: Detection is deferred to a future concrete theory. No null is predicted (contrast #11 §13 row 7).

quote: For example, such unusual non-local quanta could be found in recent reformulations of quantum gravity and string theory
where: section 4, Discussion (followed by citations of Freidel, Leigh & Minic 2013, 2014, 2015)
reading: The earliest MDM pointer to the Freidel–Leigh–Minic reformulations, offered as a possible home for the quanta. It says nothing about the quanta being the dual of visible matter. The 2010–2013 MDM texts contain no mention of Freidel, metastrings or metaparticles (my count over their full texts: 0).

quote: we plan to study the constraints from gravitational lensing and colliding clusters such as the Bullet Cluster
reading: Colliding-cluster and lensing tests are planned, not done.

quote: Modified dark matter (MDM, formerly known as MoNDian dark matter) is a phenomenological model of dark matter, inspired by quantum gravity.
reading: The authors' self-description: phenomenological.

quote: Unlike cold dark matter models, the MDM mass profile depends on the baryonic mass.
reading: The defining contrast with CDM is a baryon-dependent profile, not a stated interaction.

quote: how strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter and how does MDM self-interact?
where: section 1, list of future work, item 2
reading: In 2016 the strength of MDM's coupling to baryons and its self-interaction are open questions, listed with 'unusual particle phenomenology?' and the Bullet Cluster. MDM states no coupling beyond gravity, and does not rule one out.

quote: We show that dynamical and observed masses agree in a sample of 93 galactic clusters.
reading: Data: 93 X-ray clusters (White, Jones & Forman 1997, as analysed by Sanders 1999). Sanders found ⟨M_N/M_obs⟩ ≈ 4.4 and ⟨M_MOND/M_obs⟩ ≈ 2.1. With the general profile M′ = [ξ(a0/a) + (1/π)(a0/a)²]M and a universal ξ ≈ 0.5, the paper gets ⟨M_MDM/M_obs⟩ ≈ 1.0, and refitting the galaxies with ξ = 0.5 gives nearly identical fits with M/L lower by about 35%. Strong lensing 'appears' sufficient because a0 = cH0 = 2πa_c ≈ 6a_c (2π = 6.28 by code).

quote: Note added: This discussion has since been superseded by more recent work by the authors.
reading: The ξ-profile is superseded by the α/(1 + r/r_MDM) form of 1601.00662.

quote: The defining feature of the MDM proposal is that the modified dark matter profile should be sensitive to the fundamental acceleration
reading: The sentence continues: 'or alternatively, to the cosmological constant, at all scales (galactic, cluster and cosmological) and that on galactic scales the modified dark matter mass profile should be correlated to the baryonic mass profile' (second part code-checked FOUND). The correlation is a property required of the profile.

quote: However, we also aim to have enough flexibility not to correlate the dark matter mass profile to the baryonic mass profile on cluster and cosmological scales.
reading: The correlation is meant to switch off on cluster and cosmological scales. That is the scale limit in which it vanishes (Q4).

quote: On the other hand, this correlation could be pointing to a yet unknown property of DM which connects its distribution to that of baryonic matter.
reading: The data behind 'correlation': the RAR with ā0 = (1.20 ± 0.02)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² and the BTFR with A = (47 ± 6) M⊙ s⁴/km⁴, against 63 from MOND's normalization. By code, 1/(ā0G) = 62.8 M⊙ s⁴/km⁴, and A = 47 ± 6 implies a0 = 1.60 (1.42–1.84)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s².

quote: since some dispersion might be expected between the collision-less CDM particles, and the free baryons that act as fuel for the star formation. Nevertheless, it may be possible to reconcile this result with CDM models
reading: The authors allow that the correlation might be reproduced in gravity-only CDM with dissipative baryons (refs. 87, 58).
correction: The concession is accurate, but it sits under the authors' framing two paragraphs earlier: 'The second, and in our view more serious, tension is the set of observations at the galactic scale which strongly suggests that DM may not simply be extra, independent degrees of freedom.' (§1, FOUND). The same item also calls the correlation 'difficult to motivate within purely collision-less CDM'. The authors allow a CDM reconciliation; their own stated view is the other way.

quote: Here we emphasize one very important point. Given the fact that we have not changed Einstein's equations, we cannot change the Newton law of motion.
reading: Einstein's equations and Newton's law of motion are unchanged.

quote: To summarize: dark matter exists in our scheme, but its mass profile is tied to the baryonic mass profile (at least on galactic scales) via the observed acceleration and the fundamental acceleration parameter, set by the cosmological constant.
reading: The tie runs through a_obs and a0 within unchanged dynamics (Eq. 36: a_obs = G(M + M′)/r², with M′/M = ½a0²/[(a_obs + a0)² − a0²]).

quote: Such dark matter is most probably of a non-local, non-particle kind, because of the fact that its mass profile is tied to the baryonic mass profiles as well as to the inertial properties, encoded in the observed acceleration.
reading: The inference runs from the profile to the quanta: because the profile is tied to the baryons and to inertia, the quanta must be non-local.

quote: But what is the microscopic basis for this correlation? We will now argue that it may have something to do with the quanta of MDM being non-local (and non-particle-like)
reading: The review's own answer to Q4: the microscopic basis of the correlation is sought in the quanta's non-locality and infinite statistics, not in an interaction.
correction: The sentence before it defines 'this correlation' as the profile's sensitivity to Λ: Eqs. (3) and (35) 'indicate that modified dark matter profile is sensitive to the cosmological constant, or equivalently, the Hubble parameter.' (FOUND). So §4 gives non-locality as the basis of the dark-matter–Λ link, not of the dark–baryon tie. The review links the dark–baryon relation to the metaparticle zero-mode sector (§5, 'perhaps naturally') and, in §2.2, infers non-locality from the tie. The reading 'not in an interaction' stands.

quote: It is very hard to see why the mass profiles coming from particle-like quanta of some local effective field theory would be sensitive to a fundamental acceleration parameter, set by the cosmological scale, even if one assumes some unusual dissipative baryonic dynamics.
reading: Their reason for excluding local particles. My observation: this sits uneasily with section 1, where dissipative baryonic dynamics 'may' reconcile the data with CDM.
correction: The reader's own observation, that §4 'sits uneasily with section 1', overstates the tension. Section 1 grants a possible CDM reconciliation, but it states the authors' view that the data strongly suggest 'DM may not simply be extra, independent degrees of freedom'. It also says the a0 dependence 'has to go beyond the classical Einstein theory and the usual local effective quantum field theory' (§1, FOUND). Section 4 is consistent with both statements.

quote: At the moment the MDM proposal is not rooted in any fundamental physics, and there is no specific candidate for the MDM quantum.
reading: In September 2017 there is no candidate quantum.

quote: We expect that such non-local excitations (as part of a covariant non-commutative formulation, as implied by the metastring [131, 132]) can serve as unusual dark matter quanta.
reading: A proposal ('we expect') that non-local excitations of the metastring's non-commutative formulation serve as MDM quanta.

quote: Roughly, the zero mode sector looks like two entangled particles, and it could be viewed as a model for modified dark matter quanta discussed in this review, implying, perhaps naturally, the observed relation between dark matter and baryonic mass profiles at certain scales.
where: section 5 (footnote 13: 'metaparticles', theory being developed by Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman, Leigh and Minic)
reading: The metastring zero-mode sector as a model of MDM quanta. 'Entangled' means the two particles of that sector, and their entanglement is offered ('perhaps') as the origin of the dark–baryon profile relation. This is not yet the identification of dark matter as the dual of visible matter.

quote: How strongly coupled is MDM to baryonic matter? How does MDM self-interact?
reading: In 2017 the coupling strength and the self-interaction are still open. Contrast #11 §8, where a velocity-gated self-interaction defines the χ form.

quote: which may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed to detect dark matter particles
reading: A hedged ('may') explanation of the null results by non-locality.

quote: A more concrete theory for MDM quanta will allow us to test the whole scheme of MDM at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments.
reading: Tests at colliders and in direct and indirect detection are deferred to a concrete theory. No permanent null is stated (contrast #11 §13 row 7).

quote: it is possible that there are (dark) stars made of such quanta
reading: A speculation, conditional on infinite statistics. No condensate, wave form or momentum localization is proposed.

quote: Note that we will be treating the dark energy as the cosmological constant or vacuum energy
reading: In MDM dark energy is Λ (w = −1) throughout. Contrast #11 §10 (τ, strictly w ≥ −1, thawing).

quote: Our central observation is that Milgrom's scaling implies a non-local mixing of physics in the dark matter and dark energy sector.
reading: The dark matter–dark energy link is a0 ↔ Λ. Section 4 speculates: 'Conceivably it is the extended nature of the MDM quanta that connects them to the cosmological constant/dark energy and the Hubble parameter' (code-checked FOUND).

quote: for such extended excitations the change in momentum is proportional to the change in distance
reading: A heuristic: δp ∼ αδx together with the ordinary Heisenberg relation δpδx ∼ ħ gives an acceleration ∝ 1/distance, 'exactly what the Milgrom scaling demands'. Momentum here is ordinary momentum at ħ, and there is no conjugate polarization (contrast #11 P2′).

quote: The black squares are 386 data points from a sample of 30 galaxies presented in this paper.
reading: Data: 386 points from the 30 galaxies, fitted with a_obs = a_bar/[1 − exp(−√(a_bar/zā0))]. For the 13 clusters, values of α between ∼50 and 100 fit, values ≲50 do not, and α = 50 is used in the figures. The abstract claims 'the same critical acceleration appears both in the galactic and cluster data fits based on MDM' (code-checked FOUND, abstract), with α changing from ∼1 to 50–100 (§3.2 calls this an effective 'renormalizaton' of a0).

quote: The aforementioned MDAR indicates a coupling between DM and BM governed by a universal acceleration scale
reading: Here the authors call the mass-discrepancy acceleration relation a 'coupling' between dark and baryonic matter, without saying of what kind. Nothing in the paper makes it a force or an interaction term.

quote: One of the attributes of the MDM model is that it must decouple from baryons at the cosmological scale. Exactly how this de-coupling occurs is currently under investigation.
reading: The 'coupling' must vanish at cosmological scales, and how is unknown. The paper adds 'Since baryons should not be sensitive to' Λ, the a0 in the data is attributed to the dark matter (code-checked FOUND).

quote: We do not, however, expect the correlation between DM and BM to be as tight in galaxy clusters as it is in galaxies.
reading: The cluster correlation is looser: 13 clusters, and 12 with M2500 for the M_dyn–M_bar plot ('the correlation is not very tight').

quote: the correlations could be pointing to yet unknown properties of DM which connects its distribution to that of BM at galactic scales, yet allows for de-coupling at cosmological scales.
reading: Again a property of dark matter, not a specified interaction.

quote: This is true for galaxies, but we do not expect an acceleration floor in galaxy clusters.
reading: A prediction: an acceleration floor ∝ a0 in galaxies, none in clusters, where accelerations should fall off as 1/r.

quote: Thus, MDM quanta are not particle-like, but might be modeled as metaparticles, excitations of metastrings, which look roughly like two entangled particles in momentum space.
where: section 5, Discussion (last paragraph; cites [57] arXiv:1707.00312 and [58] arXiv:1706.03305)
reading: December 2017: a speculation ('might be modeled') that MDM quanta are metaparticles, 'two entangled particles in momentum space'. The two cited Freidel–Leigh–Minic papers mention neither dark matter nor entanglement (0 matches each, by grep of their full texts), so the dark-matter link is these authors' own. 'Momentum space' is not defined, and the paper does not say that the second particle is a dual of a visible particle. This is the earliest MDM text I found that puts the quanta in momentum space; the record does not mention the paper.

quote: The properties of CDM are completely unknown, and the only assumptions are that it is non-relativistic (Cold) and that it only interacts with the baryonic matter (and itself) gravitationally.
reading: The essay's definition of CDM: it interacts with baryons gravitationally only.

quote: are strongly correlated via an acceleration scale which appears to be universal to all spiral galaxies
reading: 'Correlated' means the observed galactic relations: the BTFR and the RAR, with a§ = (1.2 ± 0.02 (stat) ± 0.24 (syst))×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² from 2693 points in 153 SPARC galaxies (McGaugh et al. 2016). The essay adds: 'A correlation between the total dark matter and total baryonic matter in a region surrounding a galaxy is to be expected in the' ΛCDM scenario (code-checked FOUND); what surprises the authors is a universal acceleration surviving galaxies' dynamic histories.

quote: We would like to emphasize here we are quoting an observational fact, which is independent of any theoretical assumptions or biases one may have about the dynamics responsible.
reading: The correlation is presented as an observation, independent of dynamics (footnote 4: 'we are NOT pushing MOND').

quote: At this point in time, Occam's razor would favor the first option
where: essay text, after the two possibilities
reading: The first option is 'The scale is emergent in the' ΛCDM model (code-checked FOUND), supported by simulations consistent with the MDAR and BTFR [35, 36]. The second is a new property of CDM, possibly a link between dark matter and dark energy, with MDM as the authors' example ('In MDM, the CDM quanta is informed of the cosmological constant' via gravitational thermodynamics, code-checked FOUND). For galaxies the authors prefer, for now, the gravity-only option. This weighs against reading the correlation as evidence of a non-gravitational tie.
correction: The Occam preference concerns galaxies, and the essay turns from it at once: 'However, what if the same acceleration scale appeared in structures at vastly larger length-scales as well?' (FOUND; v1 has 'different' for 'larger'). For clusters it calls the emergent account hard: 'it is difficult to imagine that any' memory of a0 'would be maintained or transferred to the cluster intact' (FOUND). The abstract, already in v1, concludes that the multi-scale presence 'strongly supports the existence of a fundamental acceleration scale governing the observed gravitational physics' (FOUND, abstract). The essay ends open: 'On the other hand, it could still be that' a0 emerges in ΛCDM. 'For galaxies the authors prefer, for now, the gravity-only option' is right. 'This weighs against reading the correlation as evidence of a non-gravitational tie' holds for galaxies only; for clusters the essay leans toward a fundamental scale, though it never calls the tie non-gravitational.

quote: In Ref. [41], Zhang et al. analyze 62 of the 64 galaxy clusters in the HIFLUGCS database
reading: Data: 62 HIFLUGCS clusters (13439 member galaxies), 56 elliptical galaxies (Belli et al. 2014) and 56 globular clusters (Meylan & Pryor). σ⁴/(Ga0) clusters around M_bar, giving the BFJR with n = 4 over M_bar = 10^{4∼14} M⊙.

quote: Let us speculate: The BTFR and BFJR imply that the dark matter mass profile knows about the baryonic mass profile, the acceleration scale
reading: What follows is explicitly labelled a speculation.

quote: The dark-matter quanta are therefore inherently non-local. A possible candidate for such quanta are metaparticles, which are found in the long-distance limit of an intrinsically non-commutative formulation of quantum gravity/string theory
where: essay text, final paragraphs (cites [50], the Freidel–Leigh–Minic and Freidel–Kowalski-Glikman–Leigh–Minic papers)
reading: Metaparticles as 'a possible candidate', inside the speculation. The passage is already in v1 (18 May 2020).

quote: In this context, dark matter is correlated to the visible baryonic matter via a fundamental length scale that can be related to dark energy
where: essay text, final paragraphs (cites [51] Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2019 and [52] Minic arXiv:2003.00318)
reading: The correlation is said to run through a fundamental length related to dark energy, citing the string-side papers. No mechanism is given here, and the essay never calls the correlation non-gravitational.

quote: we would expect that there will be no evidence for it in colliding clusters
reading: A discriminator: if a0 is the end product of relaxation, colliding clusters should not show it, and its presence there 'would be very strong evidence' that a0 is fundamental. It is a test that could separate a fundamental dark–baryon tie from gravity-only dark matter.

quote: is implicit in the baryonic Tully-Fisher and baryonic Faber-Jackson relations, independently of any theoretical preference or bias
reading: An observational paper. Numbers: the BTFR slope a§ = (1.6 ± 0.2)a0 with a0 ≡ 10⁻¹⁰ m/s²; for ellipticals with globular clusters a∅ = (1.5 +1.4/−0.7)a0 (Farouki et al. 1983); 64 HIFLUGCS clusters, with gas masses and dispersions from Zhang et al.

quote: though we can see from inspection that the n=4 line is not a bad fit either, especially when one notes that potentially large systematic errors are not shown.
reading: Against-evidence stated by the authors: the clusters alone prefer n ≈ 3 ('Thus, the galaxy cluster data prefers an' n ≈ 3 BFJR, code-checked FOUND). n ≈ 4 appears when ellipticals are added (a∅ ≈ 1.4a0) and when globular clusters are added too (a∅ ≈ 1.3a0).

quote: The simplest one is, of course, that it is emergent in the standard
reading: The authors' simplest explanation of a0 is emergence in ΛCDM, with N-body evidence for spirals.
correction: The same paragraph qualifies 'simplest'. It adds 'We are not aware of similar results for ellipticals' and that the appearance of a0 'in simulations does not immediately mean an understanding of why the same' a0 'emerges over many decades of scale' in ΛCDM (FOUND). The abstract concludes that the result 'could be pointing to a heretofore unknown property of dark matter' (FOUND, abstract).

quote: proposes a DM which is made aware of
where: section V (refs. 66–68, the MDM papers; the sentence ends 'Λ via gravitational thermodynamics')
reading: MDM appears only as one model that modifies the dark-matter side. The paper contains no dual sector, metaparticle or Born geometry (counts 0), though it was posted seven months after Minic 2020.

quote: Both modified DM and modified gravity theories have a variety of phenomenological constraints that must be evaded, and it remains to be seem if any of these theories are successful in explaining BTFR and BFJR.
reading: No theory, MDM included, is said to succeed yet ('seem' as printed).

quote: we discuss a possible relationship between the acceleration scale and the quantum pressure of fuzzy dark matter models
reading: The MDM line turns to wave (fuzzy) dark matter. The essay never names MDM.

quote: particles, perhaps axion-like, with de Broglie wavelength around
reading: Standard fuzzy dark matter: ultralight (10⁻²² eV) particles with de Broglie wavelength (10²–10³) pc, treated as a Madelung fluid with a quantum potential. The essay contains no dual field, metaparticle, metastring, Born geometry or non-commutativity (counts 0).

quote: This is an interesting acceleration scale, of the same order as the acceleration scale observed in the Tully-Fisher and Faber-Jackson relations.
reading: The paper gives a_FDM ∼ 2×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² for m ∼ 10⁻²² eV and λ_dB ∼ 300 pc. By code, ħ²/(m²λ³) = 4.4×10⁻¹⁰ m/s², or 2.2×10⁻¹⁰ with the ½ in V_Q.

quote: with the gravitational potential providing a link between the baryonic and dark matter, which ultimately leads to the Tully-Fisher relation
where: essay text, FDM paragraph (reporting Lee, Kim & Lee 2019)
reading: Central to Q4: in the school's 2024 account the dark–baryon link is the gravitational potential, a gravity-only tie like that of #11 P4. Nothing beyond gravity is invoked.

quote: Similarly, by self-consistency of the above equations of motion, baryons share the same universal acceleration, because of the fact that they move in a self-consistent gravitational potential that is balanced by the quantum potential.
reading: Baryons inherit a0 by moving in the same gravitational potential.

quote: We further conjecture a relationship between the quantum pressure and dark energy, which could explain why
reading: A conjecture (the sentence ends 'a0 ∼ cH0/(2π)'). The quantum potential evaluated on the vacuum wave-functional gives the vacuum energy, whose scale 10⁻³ eV is put at the geometric mean of the Hubble (10⁻³⁴ eV) and Planck (10²⁸ eV) scales, citing Freidel–Kowalski-Glikman–Leigh–Minic 2023 and Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2023. By code √(10⁻³⁴·10²⁸) = 1.0×10⁻³ eV.

quote: could be associated with the heavier soliton degrees of freedom of FDM that are responsible for the structure of FDM halos
reading: A 10⁻¹⁹ eV scale, the geometric mean of the Hubble and vacuum scales (by code 3.2×10⁻¹⁹ eV), is tied to FDM solitons, the cores of fuzzy halos in position space. They are not magnetic and not localized in momentum (contrast #11 §12's third candidate).

quote: the current data are consistent with no change in acceleration scale with redshift
reading: Data: the RAR of 100 RC100 galaxies at z ≈ 0.5–2.5; BTFR a0 = (1.3 ± 0.3)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² (McGaugh 2012); slow-rotator E0 galaxies a0 = (1.5 +0.9/−0.6)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² (Chae et al. 2020). The proposed test: a0 should change with z, and studying that 'at higher z could provide a test of these ideas' (code-checked FOUND).
correction: The redshift test does not by itself separate the essay's fuzzy-dark-matter account from CDM. The same paragraph says 'CDM simulations indicate that the acceleration scale increases with redshift, though the amount of change depends on details of the feedback implementation.' (FOUND). Both accounts expect a0 to change with z, and the data show no change to z ∼ 2.5.

quote: Like their visible particle cousins, dark matter quanta should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter
where: section 5, Quantum gravity, metaparticles and dark matter
reading: Detection through 'metaparticle entanglement', which the next words point to in Eq. (47) as the term α′A_μ dÃ^μ/dt, 'say, for a photon and its dual'.

quote: This is a Berry-phase like term that comes from a fully covariant description, and is uniquely different from the usual effective field theory interaction terms between visible and dark matter particles. Such dark matter quanta are correlated to visible matter and have been discussed in the literature as Modified dark matter
reading: The non-gravitational link is a Berry-phase-like term, said to differ from effective-field-theory interactions, and Minic identifies the quanta it correlates with MDM's. The term comes from the string side; it is not in the MDM papers.

quote: Modified dark matter (MDM) is, at the moment, a phenomenological model of dark matter, inspired by gravitational thermodynamics.
reading: Even where it is joined to the dual sector, MDM is described as phenomenological.

quote: In particular, the natural model for MDM quanta could be provided by the metaparticle realizations of the Standard Model particles, associated with bi-local extensions of all Standard Model fields.
reading: The step the MDM papers never take. MDM quanta become the metaparticle realizations of Standard Model particles, and the next sentence gives the baryons 'natural cousins (the Ã backgrounds ...) in the dark matter sector', sensitive to Λ. It is a proposal ('could').

quote: In what follows, we argue the dual part of the matter sector appears as dark matter, which is in turn both sensitive to dark energy [18] and also dynamically correlated with the visible matter.
reading: Reference [18] is the MDM papers (Ho–Minic–Ng 2010–2012; Edmonds et al. 2014, 2017). The dark matter's 'sensitivity to dark energy' is taken from MDM.

quote: In other words, in the observable spacetime, the visible sector and its dual/dark counterpart are “mixed/correlated” (19), in a way that is sensitive to both the UV and IR cutoffs. This correlation becomes invisible in effective field theory, and it vanishes as either
reading: The correlation is a mixing term in the action, −(λ⁸/L¹⁰)f^a_b[[A_a, Ã^b]] (Eq. 19; similar terms for scalars and fermions), coupling visible and dual fields otherwise than by gravity. It vanishes as λ → 0 or L → ∞.

This is a Berry-phase-like effect that comes from a fully covariant description, and is uniquely different from the usual effective field theory interaction terms between visible and dark matter particles.
