That essay does not make the identification; its fuzzy dark matter is an ordinary ultralight boson tied to baryons by gravity. In HM, 'fuzzy' also means non-commutativity of visible and dual fields (§3: the visible and dark fields 'do not commute. Therefore, one could say that dark matter is fuzzy').

quote: In so doing, T-duality is cast essentially as a Fourier transform.
reading: The letter's founding analogy: T-duality as a Fourier transform of string-loop functionals, Ψ̃[y(σ)] = ∫[Dx(σ)] exp((1/2πi)∫x dy) Ψ[x(σ)]; 'in the compact case, the Fourier transform is just implementing the T-duality'. It is the string analog of #11 §3's ρ implemented by the Fourier transform, acting on loop functionals. The record quotes this sentence (notes/literature-check.md §3).

quote: The momentum may now be expressed as p=\oint_{C}\mathrm{d}Y , and so we will refer to Y as coordinates in momentum space.
where: paragraph 'Quasi-Periodicity and generalized T-duality' (dual Polyakov path integral)
reading: Y is called a momentum-space coordinate because its loop integral, its period around the string, is the momentum p. This is the sentence flag 64 quotes for 'the dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x'; in context it names the T-dual coordinate (next statements), not the conjugate of x.
correction: In context Y enters as the variable of the loop-space Fourier transform, Psi~[Y(sigma)] = Int[DX] exp((1/2 pi i) Int X dY) Psi[X], so as a field it is the Fourier partner of X(sigma): d_sigma Y = P is X's momentum density. 'Not the conjugate of x' holds for the zero modes (1706.03305 eq. 69: canonical pairs (p, x) and (pt, xt - pi alpha' p)); but 1706.03305 sec. 4.2 says that 'xt/{2 pi lambda^2} plays the role of the variable conjugate to x' on the reduced (x, xt) space.

quote: Moreover these quasi-periodic functions are constrained to carry no dual-momenta
reading: The 'dual-momenta' are the quasi-periods p̄ of X, i.e. windings (the letter writes p̄ = −α′∮*dY = 0). The letter's 'dual' is T-duality's exchange of momentum and winding.

quote: Now, as suggested by the preceding discussion, we can introduce a momentum space coordinate Y such that \partial_{\sigma}Y=P . Like X , this coordinate is not periodic; its quasi-period Y(2\pi)-Y(0) represents the string momentum.
where: paragraph 'First order formalism and the phase space action'
reading: Y is defined by ∂σY = P, the momentum density (α′P = ∂τX in the same paragraph); its quasi-period is the momentum. This is the T-dual field: 1706.03305 defines X̃ by ∂σX̃ = ∂τX, and Y = X̃/α′ up to a function of τ (checked symbolically in work/dual-sector/scratch/r6-foundations/dual_field.py: quasi-period of Y = 2πp). Y's zero mode is therefore the x̃ that 1706.03305 finds independent of p and non-commuting with x. #11 P4–P5 work in one phase space (x, p); the letter's 'momentum space' is the T-dual coordinate of a string.

quote: \eta is a neutral metric and H a generalized Lorentzian one
where: paragraph 'First order formalism and the phase space action', before eq. (3)
reading: FLM's generalized metric H is Lorentzian. #11 P1 takes H positive, and #11 §5 states the compatibility theorem it attributes to FLM for positive H (contradicts_record, last entry).

quote: in which Born reciprocity is implemented as a choice of a Lagrangian submanifold of the phase space, and amounts to a generalization of T-duality.
reading: Born reciprocity ('Born duality' in later FLM papers) is implemented as a choice of Lagrangian submanifold, the polarization language of #11 §3 and P5; the choice is said to generalize T-duality.

quote: In this formulation both elements (\eta,J) of the chiral structure are dynamical. The solutions are labelled by bi-Lagrangians and spacetime is a derived dynamical concept.
reading: The earliest statement in this set that η is dynamical (26 July 2013), 19 months before 1502.08005, which #11 P2′ cites for it. 'Derived dynamical concept' is not spontaneous breaking: the text has no potential, order parameter or vacuum selection ('spontan' and 'order parameter': zero matches in the full text).

quote: Note that the 2d electrostatic picture of the correlation functions of the usual vertex operators [6] (see also [8]) now generalizes to 2d electromagnetism with electric and magnetic charges (dyons), if we allow vertices with both p,\bar{p} . The corresponding Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint in the presence of these operators [15].
where: end of paragraph 'Quasi-Periodicity and generalized T-duality'
reading: The letter's only magnetic content: on the worldsheet, vertex operators carrying momentum p and winding p̄ act as 2d electric and magnetic charges, and their Dirac–Schwinger–Zwanziger quantization is the diffeomorphism (level-matching) constraint. These are string states, not magnetic monopoles in spacetime or in momentum space, and have no dark-matter role. My reading: a published remark relating the DSZ pairing to the momentum–winding pairing of string states, which bears on #11 §11.3's charge-lattice identification (flag 67), not on §11.4 or §12.

quote: Given the interpretation of X and Y , this means that not only will space-time become curved, but momentum space as well. This then will lead to an implementation of Born reciprocity.
reading: Letting H and η depend on both X and Y curves momentum space as well as spacetime: FLM's form of 'momentum space has its own gravity' (#11 App. A item 10), stated without field equations.

quote: when we talk about phase space, we do not mean the phase space of gravitational fields; we refer exclusively to the phase space of matter probes.
reading: FLM's phase space is the phase space of matter probes, as #11 P1's is of matter; gravitational fields are excluded.

quote: It is important to appreciate that this kinematical breaking is different from the dynamical breaking that arises in Schrödinger’s quantum mechanics, due to the choice of a particular Hamiltonian.
reading: FLM call the breaking of Born's symmetry by gravity 'kinematical' (the preceding sentence: Born noticed 'that the kinematical symmetry generated by I is fundamentally broken in the presence of gravity'), as opposed to breaking by a choice of Hamiltonian. This is the sense of #11 §3's 'They treat the breaking as kinematical': it describes general relativity, which FLM propose to change (§1.3 below).

quote: There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis.
reading: The preferred-polarization idea in May 2014, before the 1502.08005 sentence #11 §3 quotes.
correction: Date and wording right, but the passage presents the breaking as Born's: 'One of the central insights of Born, 75 years ago [3], was to notice that the kinematical symmetry generated by I is fundamentally broken in the presence of gravity' ([3] = Born 1935, 1938, 1949). 'There is a preferred basis' glosses Born's point; this bears on #11 sec. 3, which credits the idea to FLM.

quote: In pure quantum mechanics, H is a kinematical structure, while \eta or the choice of preferred polarization, can be modified by unitary dynamics. Alternatively, in pure gravity \eta is a kinematical structure (space-time provides a preferred polarization that cannot be modified), while H , or at least its space-time part, becomes dynamical.
reading: Two regimes: in quantum mechanics H is fixed and η (the polarization) can be changed by unitary transformations; in gravity η is fixed and spacetime is a polarization that cannot be modified. Compare #11 P2′ (ω rigid, η emergent) and P5 (vacuum selection).

quote: Moreover if we introduce quantum theory in gravity, we have to make \eta dynamical. This is our addition to Born’s argument [1].
reading: Dynamical η is claimed as FLM's own addition to Born ([1] = 1307.7080). #11 P2′ attributes 'η dynamical' to [26S] (1502.08005, 2015).

quote: Therefore a dynamical \eta necessarily leads to a relaxation of locality and a breakdown of effective field theory.
reading: My reading: FLM use a dynamical η to relax locality (relative locality); #11 §3 uses an emergent η to explain why one polarization, and with it local physics, is selected. The same move serves opposite ends.

quote: Moreover, the purely kinematical splitting of phase space into space and momentum space has to be made dynamical, and thus both the phase space metric H_{AB} and the neutral metric \eta_{AB} have to be dynamical in the context of quantum gravity.
reading: The split into space and momentum space 'has to be made dynamical'. FLM's proposal is therefore not kinematical; it is dynamical without a selection mechanism (no potential, no order parameter, no 'spontan' in the text). Qualifies #11 §3 (contradicts_record).

quote: not only a fundamental length scale \lambda but also a fundamental energy scale \varepsilon from which we can reconstruct \hbar=\lambda\varepsilon and G_{N}\propto\lambda/\varepsilon (in D=4 )
reading: Two scales: a length λ and an energy ε with ℏ = λε and G_N ∝ λ/ε in four dimensions. The momentum half of phase space is measured in units of ε (§2: 𝕏 = (X/λ, P/ε)).

quote: This means that G_{N} can be considered as a universal conversion factor between the seemingly different concepts of space and momentum space, in the same way that the speed of light is a universal conversion factor between space and time.
reading: Newton's constant as the conversion factor between space and momentum space: the essay's reason for a second fundamental scale besides ℏ.

quote: This null subspace is the effective space-time experienced by the string solution and is defined to be the Lagrangian sub-manifold with K=+1 . In this sense, different strings propagate in different space-time backgrounds which are made consistent via string interactions and through a dynamical momentum space [6], thus giving a sharp example of relative locality [5].
reading: Each string solution lives on the η-null Lagrangian with K = +1, and different strings can live on different spacetimes, reconciled by interactions (relative locality). My reading: the closest these papers come to #11 P4's matter in another polarization; it is said of all probes, with no separate matter sector and no dark matter.

quote: Since schematically \Box_{\eta}H=\partial_{X}\partial_{P}H , the last equation essentially says that the phase space metric can depend only on X or only on P . In the first case, we recover the usual graviton mode propagation on this space-time.
reading: Linearized background equations □_H H = 0, □_H η = 0, □_η H = 0; the last makes H depend only on X or only on P, the first case being the usual graviton. The second case, a metric mode on momentum space, is implied and not discussed (my reading): the nearest statement in these papers to #11 §7 and App. A item 10.

quote: Similarly, it has been argued that dynamical momentum space associated with Born reciprocity implies dramatic phenomenological consequences in the context of the vacuum energy problem [9], which also exhibits the mixing of short and long distance scales.
reading: The essay's only cosmology-adjacent remark, a pointer via ref. [9] to Chang, Lewis, Minic, Takeuchi 2011 (arXiv:1106.0068) and Chang, Minic, Takeuchi 2010 (arXiv:1004.4220). Nothing on w or on a dual spacetime's curvature.

quote: In quantum gravity, if all probes agree on what we mean by space-time, then we have broken Born duality — there is a preferred choice of polarization, the space-time one.
reading: The sentence #11 §3 quotes, verified. The breaking is the existence of a polarization shared by all probes ('absolute locality' in the next sentences); no mechanism is given.

quote: to unify both X^{\mu} and Y_{\mu} in one space {\cal{P}} (that we often refer to as phase space) and introduce a dimensionless coordinate \mathbb{X} on {\cal{P}}
reading: The metastring's 'phase space' is the doubled target (X, Y) of double field theory, the same doubling as the metaparticle's Born geometry (x, x̃), not #11's (x, p). Bears on the record's contrast between foundations and metaparticle (contradicts_record).
correction: The doubling is right, but FLM present Y as a momentum: 'Y can be thought of as a momentum coordinate' (sec. 2, after eq. 4); the dual action is 'the Polyakov action for the momentum variable' and X -> Y 'corresponds to the string Fourier transformation' (after eq. 6); Lt is 'energy-momentum' (sec. 2); sec. 7.1 calls the (X,Y) parametrization, with cell area hbar, 'the natural metastring parameterization'. 'Not #11's (x, p)' holds for the zero-mode structure (Y's zero mode is independent of p), not for FLM's own reading of Y.

quote: \lambda is the string length which is related to the slope parameter by \lambda^{2}\equiv\alpha^{\prime}\hbar , where \hbar is the Planck constant of the worldsheet quantum theory.
reading: λ² ≡ α′ℏ in this paper; 1706.03305 and 1707.00312 use λ² = ℏα′/2.

quote: we can reconstruct \hbar=\lambda\varepsilon,\qquad\alpha^{\prime}=\lambda/\varepsilon.
reading: ℏ = λε and α′ = λ/ε.

quote: The Newton constant is proportional to the latter scale, G_{N}=\rho\alpha^{\prime} , depending on the dimension and the details of compactification.
reading: Newton's constant is set by the string slope; nothing here on how a dual sector gravitates.

quote: Note that X has the dimension of length while Y has the dimension of momentum.
reading: Y has the dimension of momentum: the 'momentum-like' half of the doubled space.

quote: Indeed, as we will see, for a boundary located at fixed \tau , \partial_{\sigma}X^{\mu} and Y_{\mu} are conjugate variables satisfying
reading: Y is conjugate to the σ-derivative of X, {∂σX^μ(σ), Y_μ(σ′)} = 2πδ_P(σ, σ′), not to X itself. For the zero modes, x pairs with Y's period (the momentum) and Y's zero mode is a further variable (1706.03305).

quote: A choice of Lagrangian subspace of phase space is called a choice of polarization.
reading: The same definition of polarization as #11's (a Lagrangian subspace taken as position); η is called the 'polarization metric'.

quote: Here neutral means that \eta is of signature (d,d) , while H is of signature (2,2(d-1)) .
reading: H is Lorentzian here; #11 §5 states the compatibility theorem it attributes to [26S, §2.1] for positive H.

quote: In the string case if the B field vanishes H is related to \omega via a complex structure. This is no longer true if B does not vanish.
reading: The compatibility statement #11 §5 attributes to [26S, §2.1], verified; stated for the Lorentzian H of footnote 9.

quote: Thus, the usual string theory in curved backgrounds corresponds to making the Q-metric H dynamical (but not the P-metric \eta or the symplectic structure \omega ).
reading: Ordinary string theory in curved backgrounds makes only H dynamical; the metastring makes η and ω dynamical too (§2.3).

quote: However, the Born proposal is not enough. As we have pointed out in [3], in the metastring theory we must take \eta to be dynamical as well. As we have seen above, it is \eta that governs the splitting of phase space into space and momentum space.
reading: FLM credit dynamical η to their ref. [3], the 2013 letter; #11 P2′ cites this 2015 paper for it.

quote: In the general case we promote (\eta^{0},H^{0},\omega^{0})\to(\eta,H,\omega) to be functions of \mathbb{X} .
reading: All three structures become functions on P; ω is kept closed (non-closed ω is 'beyond the scope of our present discussion', §2.3). #11 P2′ keeps ω alone rigid. My remark: a closed ω that varies on P is locally constant in Darboux coordinates; the paper does not discuss ℏ in this connection.

quote: In the context of the metastring, the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric \eta , a metric in phase space that tells us how to define the notion of Lagrangian submanifolds.
reading: FLM place the rigidity of quantum theory in the flatness of η and expect it to be relaxed on curved backgrounds; #11 P2′ places it in ω (constancy of ℏ) and makes η emergent (answer 'Other: rigidity').

quote: We also clearly see that the 2-form \omega does not enter the definition of the string symplectic form. It only depends on the neutral metric \eta .
reading: The string's symplectic form on the space of solutions is built from η: {𝕏^A(σ), 𝕏^B(σ′)} = η^{AB}θ(σ − σ′) (eq. 119); ω enters only for the zero modes (1706.03305 §4.1). My reading: η plays the canonical role for string modes that ω plays in #11's point-particle phase space.

quote: That is, it relaxes the hypothesis of absolute locality and allows us to have a framework in which locality is relative, or, in colloquial terms, a framework where each string can carry a different space-time.
reading: A curved η makes the split between spacetime and momentum space non-universal. As in 1405.3949, relative locality for all probes, not a separate matter sector.

quote: The \mathbb{Z}_{2} component of the symmetry group is generated by J . This corresponds to the exchange of two Lagrangian subspaces.
reading: T-duality J, a symmetry of the flat metastring action, exchanges the two Lagrangians (also §8: 'T-duality exchanges the Lagrangian sub-manifold with its orthogonal complement'). The other choice is equally lawful in the flat theory, as #11 P5 says of the mirror vacuum.

quote: In the metastring formulation new CFT deformation modes are allowed, including the winding modes, whose collective excitations correspond to deformations of the \eta background. This links the relaxation of locality with purely stringy excitation modes.
reading: η is a dynamical background whose deformations are collective excitations of winding modes (§1 adds that vertex operators in the spectrum 'are the seeds of deformation of the polarization metric η'). No potential for η and no vacuum value are given.

quote: What is new about this viewpoint is that it allows us to think about the choice of space-time inside phase space as a dynamical question.
reading: 'A dynamical question', the phrase #11 §3 quotes, verified. The answer the paper gives is the worldsheet-locality selection of the next statement, not a vacuum mechanism.

quote: The condition of L -projectability is a target space locality condition specifying which submanifold of {\cal{P}} can be understood as a space-time. What is conceptually remarkable here is that this target space locality condition is selected by demanding worldsheet locality.
reading: What selects spacetime in the metastring: worldsheet locality selects L-projectability, a target-space locality condition; quantum mechanically it becomes Λ-periodicity (§6.4). A consistency condition; it does not prefer L over its partner (my reading).

quote: In order to formalize this intuition we define q\equiv x and p=h\tilde{y} and then we promote these variables to operators satisfying the Heisenberg algebra [p,q]=i\hbar .
reading: FLM map the doubled space onto a Heisenberg algebra with ℏ. The symbol ỹ is not defined elsewhere in the text; from context it is the dual coordinate (my reading). This is FLM's explicit reading of the dual coordinate as a momentum at ℏ.

quote: We mean that the area of the cell is \hbar , even if \lambda and \epsilon are the string length and string energy.
reading: In (X, Y) units the modular cell has area ℏ although λ and ε are string scales. Consistent with the zero-mode algebra: in the 2013 letter's momentum units, Y₀ = x̃/α′, [x, Y₀] = iπℏ (computed in scratch/r6-foundations/units.py).

quote: In the context of quantum mechanics, operators x and p do not commute and thus their eigenvalues cannot be localized within a cell of area \hbar . The modular variables [x] and [p] , on the other hand, commute with one another, and thus their eigenvalues can be specified precisely.
reading: Modular variables commute and can be specified jointly: a modular cell is a polarization that is neither position nor momentum. Bears on #11 §3's mandatory-breaking premise (answer 'Other: modular polarizations').

quote: In particular, one can easily see that, in the Heisenberg picture, the time evolution of such observables is fundamentally non-local, and that this non-locality is subtly hidden from us by the delicate interplay between the uncertainty relation and the compactness of the modular observables.
reading: Modular observables evolve non-locally (FLM follow Aharonov): modular polarizations do not give local physics in the usual sense.

quote: Any time we try to ‘compactify’ a direction we introduce a delocalization \emptyset\to[\tilde{x}] in the dual direction in a way consistent with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.
reading: Compactifying x delocalizes x̃: the x–x̃ uncertainty trade-off, the analog of #11 §3's x–p argument. No matter is localized in x̃.

quote: The usual space-time description emerges when the fields can be assumed to be approximately independent of \tilde{x} , that is when m>\!>\tilde{m} .
reading: Modular-spacetime fields carry two masses, with □Φ + □̃Φ = (m² + m̃²)Φ and ∂·∂̃Φ = m m̃Φ (eq. 233); ordinary spacetime physics when m ≫ m̃, where dependence on x̃ drops out.

quote: Consistent with the diffeomorphism constraint, we will in general have ‘dyonic states’ in the spectrum.
reading: 'Dyonic states' are string states carrying both momentum and winding monodromies, not magnetic monopoles.

quote: We expect that the metastring will offer new paradigms for particle phenomenology, for cosmology and for problems in gravity in which quantum mechanics and locality play a central role, and it may offer new insights into standard problems in string theory, such as vacuum selection.
reading: The paper's only remark on phenomenology and cosmology: no prediction, no dark sector.

quote: Given a scale, we can unify space and momentum into phase space, denoted {\cal{P}} , and introduce dimensionless coordinates x\equiv q/\lambda and \tilde{x}\equiv p/\varepsilon measuring position and momentum in natural units.
reading: Here x̃ is the momentum p of the same particle in units of ε: #11's single phase space (x, p). The only paper in this set where the dual coordinate is the conjugate momentum; it concerns ordinary quantum mechanics, not strings or dark matter.

quote: [\hat{x}^{a},\hat{\tilde{x}}_{b}]=\frac{i}{2\pi}\delta^{a}{}_{b}.
reading: [x̂, x̃̂] = i/2π, which is [q, p] = iℏ with ε = 2πℏc/λ at c = 1 (checked in scratch/r6-foundations/normalizations.py, item 3).

quote: \lambda , which in turn defines (given \hbar ) a fundamental energy scale \varepsilon=2\pi\hbar c/\lambda .
reading: Here λε = 2πℏc, against ℏ = λε in 1405.3949 and 1502.08005: the papers' normalizations differ by 2π.

quote: we propose to define Euclidean quantum space as a choice of polarization for the Heisenberg algebra of quantum theory.
reading: Quantum space is a polarization of the Heisenberg algebra (a maximal commutative *-subalgebra): FLM's general notion behind #11 P5's polarization.

quote: We show, following Mackey, that generically, such polarizations contain a fundamental length scale and that contrary to what is implied by the Schrödinger polarization, they possess topologically distinct spectra. These are the modular spaces.
reading: Generic polarizations carry a length scale and are modular, not Lagrangian (answer 'Other: modular polarizations').

quote: From this perspective, it is clear that the Schrödinger representation is not a generic representation of the Heisenberg algebra but on the other hand a highly singular one.
reading: The position (Schrödinger) polarization is a singular limit of modular ones.

quote: The concept of locality that we use in physical theories is tied to the choice of a preferred basis, the Schrödinger polarization.
reading: Locality is tied to the position polarization, consistent with #11 §3's link between local physics and a definite polarization.

quote: Thus we are led to the conclusion that general quantizations correspond to a choice of three structures, (\omega,\eta,H) where \omega is the symplectic structure that defines the Heisenberg algebra.
reading: In quantum mechanics ω defines the Heisenberg algebra (as in #11 P2′), η fixes the polarization (a bilagrangian lattice), and H the vacuum.

quote: In the context of modular polarizations, we show that there is generally no well-defined notion of translation invariant vacuum. Instead, we show that a vacuum can be identified with a state that is annihilated by a kinetic “Hamiltonian”.
reading: 'Vacuum' is the ground state of a kinetic 'Hamiltonian' built from H; changing H squeezes it (§1.7, a Bogoliubov transformation). The vacuum fixes H, not the polarization; no vacuum selects a polarization (my reading).

quote: A choice of quantum polarization is a choice of basis, unitarily equivalent to any other.
reading: A polarization is a basis choice, unitarily equivalent to any other (Stone–von Neumann). In #11 §3 and P5 it is a physical vacuum choice; here it is not physical.
correction: 'Here it is not physical' overstates. Sec. 1.4 of the same paper: the Stone-von Neumann theorem 'is in our view fundamentally misleading in the present context. It doesn't appreciate that different polarizations do have very different geometry, notions of regularity, and sets of C^infinity vectors'; the Schroedinger polarization is 'highly singular', the modular one generic. FLM hold polarizations unitarily equivalent yet physically different in these respects; what they lack is a vacuum that selects one.

quote: The space {\rm U}(d)/{\rm O}(d) represents the choice of inequivalent lifts \eta that preserve the symplectic structure and the vacuum state, while the quotient of the double orthogonal group by O (d) represent the choice of inequivalent symplectic structures, hence Weyl groups, that possess the same Hilbert space with the same vacuum.
reading: The η compatible with a fixed ω and a fixed vacuum form U(d)/O(d), the Lagrangian Grassmannian Λ(d) (a standard identification): the manifold #11 §10 (Λ(1), τ's circle) and §14 item 12 (Λ(4)) use for the polarization. FLM treat it as a set of inequivalent choices, not as a vacuum manifold.

quote: This is also the case in the double field theory picture in string theory where the target space is doubled to include winding modes but the space-time coordinate x and its dual, the winding coordinates \tilde{x} , are assumed to be commuting with each other
reading: FLM contrast their picture with double field theory, where x̃ are 'the winding coordinates' commuting with x; in the modular picture the two polarizations do not commute.

quote: it seems natural to suppose that the fundamental length scale is associated with the gravitational (or string) scale, \varepsilon/\lambda\sim c^{4}/G_{N} .
reading: A conjecture (the paper calls the interpretation 'certainly more conjectural'): the cell's scale is gravitational or stringy.

quote: This is a huge tension and all quantum experiments performed today, even the most energetic ones, fail by a huge margin to probe the thickness of the modular cell in the momentum direction. For all practical purposes we can then assume that the space is not modular, as long as we are not dealing with quantum gravity observables.
reading: Why modularity goes unseen: a Planckian cell's momentum thickness is beyond experiment. The argument concerns the modularity of space, not a dark sector or the null results of direct detection.

quote: It is quite possible that the structure of modular quantizations has observable consequences in metastring theory, through UV-IR mixing, when the appropriate limit is taken to obtain local effective field theories in large space-times.
reading: Possible observable consequences through UV–IR mixing; no specific prediction.

quote: where we have introduced the string length scale \lambda\equiv\sqrt{\frac{\hbar\alpha^{\prime}}{2}},
reading: λ = √(ℏα′/2) in this paper (λ² = α′ℏ in 1502.08005).

quote: which is such that \partial_{\sigma}\tilde{X}=\partial_{\tau}X
reading: The dual field X̃ = X_R − X_L is fixed by ∂σX̃ = ∂τX; the 2013 letter's 'momentum space coordinate' Y is X̃/α′ (dual_field.py).

quote: where x=x_{R}+x_{L} and \tilde{x}=x_{R}-x_{L} . We regard X(\tau,\sigma),\tilde{X}(\tau,\sigma) as a reorganization of X_{L}(\tau-\sigma),X_{R}(\tau+\sigma) . In particular, the zero modes (x,\tilde{x},p,\tilde{p}) should be considered independent, being linear combinations of (x_{L},p_{L},x_{R},p_{R}) .
reading: x̃ = x_R − x_L is independent of the momentum p: the program's p corresponds to FLM's p, not to x̃.

quote: In this limit, the (x,p) zero modes decouple, and \tilde{X}(\tau,\sigma) is the field that the string couples to, with \tilde{x} coordinatizing the (T-dual) non-compact geometry. The momentum p plays the role of the translational monodromy of \tilde{X}(\tau,\sigma) , i.e.,
reading: x̃ coordinatizes the T-dual geometry and p is the period of X̃: the 2013 letter's 'momentum space' direction is this x̃ direction.

quote: indicates that the operator that is canonically conjugate to \hat{\tilde{p}} is not \hat{\tilde{x}} , but instead \hat{\tilde{q}}:=\hat{\tilde{x}}-\pi\alpha^{\prime}\hat{p} . It is this operator, rather than \hat{\tilde{x}} , that commutes with \hat{x} .
reading: x̃ = q̃ + πα′p, where q̃ is conjugate to the winding p̃ and commutes with x. The πα′p part is why x and x̃ do not commute (units.py: [x, q̃] = 0, [q̃, p̃] = iℏ). x̃ is thus momentum-like in part, but it is not the canonical conjugate of x.
correction: The decomposition xt = qt + pi alpha' p and [x, qt] = 0 are verified (verify_numbers.py B). 'Not the canonical conjugate of x' holds for the Darboux pairs FLM name in eq. (69), but sec. 4.2 of the same paper says 'xt/{2 pi lambda^2} plays the role of the variable conjugate to x' (the topological term in Aharonov-Bohm form, 'the Lagrangian analog of the non-commutativity relation (69)'), the coupling making (x, xt) 'a phase space'. By my computation hbar xt/(2 pi lambda^2) = xt/(pi alpha') = p + qt/(pi alpha'), whose commutator i hbar with x comes wholly from p.

quote: The proper interpretation is that (p,x) and (\tilde{p},\tilde{x}-\pi\alpha^{\prime}p) are canonically conjugate pairs, and in particular, we should have [\hat{x},\hat{\tilde{x}}-\pi\alpha^{\prime}\hat{p}]=0 .
reading: FLM's canonical pairs: (p, x) and (p̃, x̃ − πα′p). The canonical conjugate of x is p, not x̃ (contradicts flag 64).
correction: Eq. (69) verified, but 'the canonical conjugate of x is p, not xt (contradicts flag 64)' omits sec. 4.2 of the same paper: 'xt/{2 pi lambda^2} plays the role of the variable conjugate to x'. In the full zero-mode phase space x's canonical partner is p; in the reduced (x, xt) space with symplectic form omega, xt (rescaled) is x's conjugate. Flag 64's wording has this partial support, in a paper the flag does not cite.

quote: [\hat{x}^{a},\hat{\tilde{x}}_{b}]=2\pi i\lambda^{2}\delta^{a}{}_{b},\qquad[\hat{x}^{a},\hat{p}_{b}]=i\hbar\delta^{a}{}_{b},\qquad[\hat{\tilde{x}}_{a},\hat{\tilde{p}}^{b}]=i\hbar\delta_{a}{}^{b},\qquad[\hat{p}_{a},\hat{\tilde{p}}^{b}]=0.
reading: The full zero-mode algebra; reproduced from the paper's eq. (72) in units.py ([p, x̃] = 0 and [x, p̃] = 0 as well).

quote: In particular, the operators (\hat{x},\hat{\tilde{x}}) appearing in the mode expansions do not commute, with the noncommutativity scale given by 2\pi\lambda^{2}=\pi\hbar\alpha^{\prime} .
reading: 2πλ² = πℏα′ (normalizations.py, item 1): a string-length effect in x̃'s length units; in Y's momentum units the same commutator is [x, Y₀] = iπℏ (units.py).

quote: Note that eq. (52) does not depend on the compactification radius, but only on the string length \lambda .
reading: The x–x̃ commutator does not depend on the radius; it is removed only as α′ → 0.

quote: it is only in the R\to\infty ( R\to 0 ) limit that a projection \tilde{p}\to 0 ( p\to 0 ) on the spectrum is induced, at which point \tilde{x} ( x ) decouples.
reading: Decoupling limits: large R projects p̃ → 0 and x̃ decouples; small R the reverse.

quote: Our analysis therefore confirms the results established in [7] that the double space \cal P should be understood as a phase space.
reading: FLM's thesis that the doubled space is a phase space; the record's 'momentum-like half of a doubled phase space' (notes/literature-check.md §3) states it accurately.

quote: Here, \omega_{AB} appears as the symplectic form of the \mathbb{X} zero modes.
reading: ω is the symplectic form of the zero modes 𝕏 = (x, x̃); η governs the oscillators (1502.08005 §4.2).

quote: From this point of view, the zero mode space can be considered as a phase space. Drawing an analogy with [9] then, it seems natural to conjecture that in this framework a choice of space-time corresponds to a choice of commutative subalgebra.
reading: Spacetime as a choice of commutative subalgebra, stated as a conjecture; the text goes on that the classical choices {x} or {x̃} are those 'recovered in decompactification limits', so the radius decides.

quote: Generally, T-dualities act within this framework as the operations that change the choice of polarization.
reading: T-duality is a change of polarization.

quote: \displaystyle\left[x^{a},p_{b}\right]=i\hbar\delta^{a}{}_{b},\qquad\left[\tilde{x}_{a},\tilde{p}^{b}\right]=i\hbar\delta_{a}{}^{b}.
reading: The ordinary Heisenberg pairs: [x, p] = iℏ and [x̃, p̃] = iℏ.

quote: In addition, there is an unexpected contribution to the symplectic form, equivalent to the commutator \displaystyle\left[x^{a},\tilde{x}_{b}\right]=2\pi i\lambda^{2}\delta^{a}{}_{b}, (6) and all the other commutators vanish.
reading: [x, x̃] = 2πiλ² with λ = √(ℏα′/2); all other zero-mode commutators vanish.

quote: Thus the non-commutativity of the zero modes takes a simple form, being simply a Heisenberg algebra satisfied by (x^{a},\tilde{x}_{b}) , with the string length setting the scale for the commutator.
reading: x and x̃ form a Heisenberg algebra whose scale is the string length.

quote: \omega_{AB} can be thought of as a symplectic form on the reduced space coordinatized by \mathbb{X}^{A} , a subspace of the full phase space.
reading: In FLM's own words the (x, x̃) space is 'a subspace of the full phase space', which also contains p and p̃: the doubled space sits inside a doubled phase space.

quote: It is well known that R\to\infty corresponds to decompactification where the \tilde{x} mode decouples and the effective description can be achieved in terms of space-time fields \Phi(x) .
reading: In the decompactification limit x̃ decouples and fields depend on x only.

quote: Consequently, which compact coordinate, x or \tilde{x} , plays the role of a spatial coordinate depends on context.
reading: Which coordinate is spatial depends on context: the radius selects x (large R) or x̃ (small R).

quote: and thus the coordinate \tilde{x} plays a complementary role to that of x : one should simply choose one or the other, depending on the physics that one wishes to describe, the difference being simply a change of basis.
reading: The dual tower Φ_n(x̃) carries 'precisely the same information' as Φ_w(x). My reading: the 'fields living in the dual space' (§3) are the same states in another basis, not a second population of matter.

quote: Of course, we find that this product expresses the conservation of both momentum and winding under multiplication since the total momenta n of (\Phi\circ\Psi) is given by the sum of individual momenta associated with \Phi and \Psi and similarly for the winding.
reading: The splitting–joining interaction conserves momentum and winding; its vertex carries a phase exp(iπw′(n − n′)) depending on the legs' momenta and windings (eq. 41), which FLM call a π-flux. No suppression by relative momentum, so nothing like #11 §8's gate.

quote: The algebraic structure that we are working with here has an analogy in electromagnetism in the presence of monopoles. In that analogy, the string length becomes the magnetic length, and the form \omega becomes the magnetic field.
reading: Monopoles appear only as an analogy for the zero-mode algebra (also 'the magnetic algebra of the lowest Landau level'); no magnetically charged objects.

quote: Because of its interpretation as a particle model on Born geometry, the space-time on which the metaparticle propagates is ambiguous, with different choices related by what in string theory we would call T-duality.
reading: The metaparticle's spacetime is ambiguous; the choices are related by T-duality.

quote: The metaparticle is defined in a doubled target phase space of Lorentzian signature, whose coordinates we label \{x^{\mu},p_{\mu},\tilde{x}_{\mu},\tilde{p}^{\mu}\} , with \mu=0,1,...,d-1 .
reading: A doubled phase space: x̃ is a coordinate with its own momentum p̃. #11's χ lives in the p-polarization of (x, p); the metaparticle's dual half is (x̃, p̃).

quote: The third term, which depends on an additional parameter \alpha^{\prime} , leads to non-commutativity of x^{\mu} and \tilde{x}_{\mu} , and so the phase space coordinates that we are using here are not quite Darboux coordinates. One recovers the Darboux parameterization in the limit \alpha^{\prime}\to 0 .
reading: The x–x̃ noncommutativity is an α′ effect and disappears as α′ → 0. The symplectic form, eq. (7), is ω = δp∧δx + δp̃∧δx̃ + πα′ δp∧δp̃.

These brackets follow from eq. (7) under the paper's convention (normalizations.py, item 4); with [x, p] = iℏ they give [x, x̃] = iπℏα′ = 2πiλ² in 1706.03305's λ. The record's [x, x̃] = iλ² (notes/literature-check.md §3, from Hübsch and Minic 2024) needs λ² = πℏα′.

quote: It should be clear though that there is nothing special about the x^{\mu} ; we could have taken any linear subspace, such as \tilde{x},p . Generally, other polarizations can be obtained from our analysis by generalized Fourier transforms and will be considered elsewhere.
reading: The polarization (x, p̃) is the authors' choice for the analysis; others follow by generalized Fourier transforms. A choice of representation, not a vacuum selection.

quote: this has an interesting interpretation in which the x^{\mu} coordinatize space-time, with \tilde{p}^{\mu} representing additional quantum numbers.
reading: In the (x, p̃) polarization x is spacetime and p̃ labels states.

quote: By allowing (the eigenvalues of) \tilde{p} to be non-zero, we are effectively compactifying the target space.
reading: In the string analog a non-zero p̃ is a winding.

quote: We see that the effect of the {\cal D} -constraint is to effectively fix the component of the momentum parallel to \tilde{p} .
reading: The constraint p·p̃ = μ fixes each particle's momentum along p̃: a single-particle constraint, not a dependence on the relative momentum of two particles.

quote: This shows that the usual relativistic particle can be viewed as a metaparticle which is “massless” for the \cal D constraint and which possesses vanishing external dual momentum. This sector corresponds to a consistent truncation of the theory since the vanishing of \tilde{p} is consistent with momentum conservation and is preserved by the interactions.
reading: Ordinary particles are the μ = 0, p̃ = 0 sector, a consistent truncation preserved by interactions. My inference: with p̃ conserved, a p̃ = 0 sector does not feed p̃ ≠ 0 states; a selection rule on p̃, not a gate.

quote: Note that if different metaparticles carry different non-zero values of \tilde{p} , then they have different dispersion relations and de facto effectively experience different notions of space-time even if they have the same mass. Furthermore, since \tilde{p} is conserved, the introduction of interactions implies that there must be metaparticles with distinct values of \tilde{p} .
reading: Different p̃, different dispersion, 'de facto' different spacetimes; relative locality built in. Nearest to #11 P4's matter in another polarization, but it concerns any metaparticle, and no dark matter is mentioned.

quote: This means that the metaparticle prescription |e| creates a fundamental ‘entanglement’ of these chiral particles which prevents an interpretation as two particle species.
reading: The only 'entanglement' in these papers: the two chiral components of one metaparticle, explicitly not two species. Not a relation between dark and visible matter.

quote: This duality corresponds to the exchange of p with \tilde{p} .
reading: The two positive energy roots Ω± are exchanged by Ω± = μ/Ω∓, which is the exchange of p and p̃.

quote: The first inversion means that associated to each particle there is a corresponding anti-particle, the second inversion likewise means that associated with a particle, anti-particle pair there is a corresponding dual particle, dual anti-particle pair.
reading: Each particle/antiparticle pair has a dual particle/dual antiparticle pair: further poles of the same propagator (E ↔ μ/E). No dark-matter role here (no 'dark' in the text). My reading: it is the metaparticle's only 'dual' particle content, and the record's Minic 2020 quote speaks of 'metaparticle quanta' as dark matter (not read by me).

quote: We will leave discussion of this physics to future work, and point to a second notion of interactions, in which we couple the theory to background fields.
reading: Interactions that change particle number are not developed; only background (Abelian gauge) fields are coupled. An INSPIRE title-and-abstract search for 'metaparticle' finds five papers, none of which develops them.
correction: The five hits are confirmed, but 'none of which develops them' rests on titles and abstracts: the reader read none of the other four (Minic 2020, Barnes-Heremans-Minic 2021, Chouha 2026a,b). Their abstracts, checked, develop no particle-number-changing metaparticle interaction; Barnes, Heremans and Minic state 'the Cooper mechanism is possible in the quasi-metaparticle case', a condensed-matter analog.

quote: It is useful to note that the Poisson brackets derived from (7) are reminiscent of the Dirac brackets found for charged particles in a magnetic field, reduced to the lowest Landau level.
reading: A magnetic-field analogy for the brackets; no monopoles.

quote: The Born reciprocity principle states that the validity of quantum mechanics implies a fundamental symmetry between space and momentum space. This symmetry results from the freedom to choose a basis of states. General relativity fundamentally breaks this symmetry because it states that spacetime is curved, while energy-momentum space, defined as a cotangent space, is linear and flat.
reading: FLM place the breaking of Born reciprocity in general relativity's flat momentum space, not in a vacuum. #11 §3 makes the same diagnosis ('general relativity's flat momentum fibers — the last an architectural assumption'); FLM had it in 2013.

quote: Thus, we see that it is a matter of convention that we have taken \bar{p} to vanish.
reading: For the flat string, which of X and its Fourier dual Y carries the quasi-period, and so which is read as spacetime, is a convention. The two are related by a Fourier transform, which is T-duality in the compact case. The choice is called conventional, not physical.
correction: The convention named is that the dual momentum vanishes (p̄ = 0: Y carries no dual momenta), a boundary condition. The sentence does not say that which of X or Y is spacetime is conventional; the next ones say that in the compact case the Fourier transform is T-duality and the boundary conditions can be relaxed to finite (p, p̄).

quote: And finally, we relax the condition on \eta to be a flat metric, i.e. we allow it to be arbitrary curved. These generalizations restore the Born duality symmetry.
where: 'First order formalism and the phase space action' paragraphs
reading: A curved, dynamical η is said to restore Born duality. The breaking is blamed on the fixed flat structures of the usual formulation, not on a vacuum.
correction: 'These generalizations' are three taken together: H depending on both X and Y, quasi-periods along both X and Y, and a curved η. The curved η alone is not said to restore Born duality.

quote: One can show [15] that solutions of the classical string EOM associated with a chiral structure (\eta,J) on \cal P are in correspondence with transversal bi-Lagrangian distributions.
reading: The choice of bi-Lagrangian, which fixes which Lagrangian is spacetime, labels solutions of the equations of motion. My reading: this makes the choice a property of a solution, which is where a vacuum would carry it, but FLM neither call it a vacuum choice nor analyse it as symmetry breaking.

quote: In this formulation both elements (\eta,J) of the chiral structure are dynamical. The solutions are labelled by bi-Lagrangians and spacetime is a derived dynamical concept.
reading: This is the earliest school statement found that the choice of spacetime inside phase space is dynamical (2013). The record already quotes it (notes/toy-lagrangian.md; the wiki page on broken Born duality). It gives no potential, no order parameter and no vacuum analysis.

quote: We have presented a new viewpoint on string theory, with wide ramifications and applications ranging from the stringy uncertainty principle [6, 9, 8] to “non-compact” T-duality [25], including the vacuum problem in string theory.
reading: 'The vacuum problem' here means the string-vacuum problem, listed as an application. Nothing in the letter ties it to the choice of polarization.

quote: Note that the 2d electrostatic picture of the correlation functions of the usual vertex operators [6] (see also [8]) now generalizes to 2d electromagnetism with electric and magnetic charges (dyons), if we allow vertices with both p,\bar{p} . The corresponding Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint in the presence of these operators [15].
where: 'Quasi-Periodicity and generalized T-duality', paragraph on relaxed boundary conditions
reading: These are worldsheet (2d) charges. Momentum p acts as electric charge and winding p̄ as magnetic charge of dyonic vertex operators, and their Dirac–Schwinger–Zwanziger quantization is the diffeomorphism (level-matching) constraint. They are not magnetically charged objects in spacetime or in momentum space. My comparison: this is a school precedent for #11 §11.3's symplectic charge lattice, not for §11.4.

quote: One of the central insights of Born, 75 years ago [3], was to notice that the kinematical symmetry generated by I is fundamentally broken in the presence of gravity.
reading: This is where the word 'kinematical' comes from. The Born symmetry is kinematical, and gravity breaks it. FLM credit the observation to Born.

quote: It is important to appreciate that this kinematical breaking is different from the dynamical breaking that arises in Schrödinger’s quantum mechanics, due to the choice of a particular Hamiltonian. In the latter case we can still change the basis of states.
reading: FLM separate two cases. 'Kinematical breaking' is GR's, where no change of basis is possible. 'Dynamical breaking' is the explicit breaking by a chosen Hamiltonian in quantum mechanics. Neither is spontaneous breaking in the program's sense, a symmetric law with an asymmetric vacuum.

quote: There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis. According to Born, the clash between the kinematical duality symmetry of quantum mechanics and the presence of dynamical space-time curvature is what prevents us from a theory of quantum gravity. In other words, a theory of quantum gravity ought to restore the kinematical duality principle.
reading: FLM aim to restore the duality, not to break it. Their preferred spacetime basis is a defect of GR that quantum gravity should remove. Compare #11 §3, where the breaking is mandatory and spontaneous.

quote: In pure quantum mechanics, H is a kinematical structure, while \eta or the choice of preferred polarization, can be modified by unitary dynamics. Alternatively, in pure gravity \eta is a kinematical structure (space-time provides a preferred polarization that cannot be modified), while H , or at least its space-time part, becomes dynamical.
where: §1.3 Summary: Quantum gravity and dynamical phase space
reading: η is identified with 'the choice of preferred polarization'. In GR it is kinematical; in quantum mechanics it can be changed by unitary evolution.

quote: Moreover if we introduce quantum theory in gravity, we have to make \eta dynamical. This is our addition to Born’s argument [1].
reading: FLM claim a dynamical η, the structure that encodes the polarization, as their own addition (2013–2014). #11 P2′ credits this: 'That η should be dynamical rather than fixed was argued independently in metastring theory'.

quote: It is important to note that the kinematical nature of \eta in gravity is tied up with the assumption of locality, i.e., the existence of a single well-defined space-time for all matter probes. Therefore a dynamical \eta necessarily leads to a relaxation of locality and a breakdown of effective field theory.
reading: For FLM a dynamical η relaxes locality. My comparison: in #11 §3 the selection of a polarization is what makes local physics possible ('any world with local physics must select a Lagrangian polarization'). The two treat the link between η and locality in opposite directions.
correction: 'Opposite directions' overstates. FLM tie a kinematical (fixed) η to absolute locality and say a dynamical η relaxes it; #11 §3 ties local physics to a selected polarization. Both tie locality to a definite η. The difference is that the program's vacuum fixes η, where FLM accept relaxed (relative) locality.

quote: Moreover, the purely kinematical splitting of phase space into space and momentum space has to be made dynamical, and thus both the phase space metric H_{AB} and the neutral metric \eta_{AB} have to be dynamical in the context of quantum gravity.
reading: The splitting, that is the polarization, is to be made dynamical. This is FLM's proposal, against the kinematical splitting of GR.

quote: This formulation does not require the presence of a bi-Lagrangian structure K . However when we look at solutions of string theory, we find this extra structure.
where: §2 String Theory and Dynamical Phase Space
reading: The action carries no K, the structure that tells space from momentum, but solutions do. My inference: a law without K whose solutions carry K is the logical form of a symmetry broken by the solution, the structure the program calls spontaneous breaking. FLM do not use that word, do not compare solutions by energy, and give no potential. This sentence is not in the record.

quote: This null subspace is the effective space-time experienced by the string solution and is defined to be the Lagrangian sub-manifold with K=+1 . In this sense, different strings propagate in different space-time backgrounds which are made consistent via string interactions and through a dynamical momentum space [6], thus giving a sharp example of relative locality [5].
reading: The spacetime is a property of each string solution and can differ from probe to probe (relative locality). Agreement comes from interactions. This differs from P5, where one vacuum selects for all matter.

quote: When this Lagrangian manifold is assumed to be a fixed kinematical \eta -null subspace (which requires \eta to be kinematical) then we recover the usual Polyakov formulation where all strings propagate in the same fixed Lagrangian subspace, called space-time. But we see that this special case happens only when \eta is kinematical, and not dynamical.
reading: The usual, universal spacetime is the special case of a kinematical η. FLM's general case has a dynamical η.

quote: In order to generalize one of the key properties of T-duality, it is natural to demand that J maps the space-time Lagrangian K=1 onto the momentum space Lagrangian K=-1 .
reading: T-duality (J) exchanges the spacetime and momentum-space Lagrangians, so the other choice is related to this one by a symmetry. Compare P5's 'the mirror vacuum is equally lawful'.

quote: the usual dynamical space-time picture appears only as an induced concept (the choice of a Lagrangian submanifold in a dynamical bi-Lagrangian structure) on equal footing with its complementary and likewise induced dynamical momentum space picture (the choice of a dual Lagrangian submanifold in the same dynamical bi-Lagrangian structure).
reading: The spacetime and momentum-space pictures are 'on equal footing', and both are induced by a choice inside a dynamical structure.

quote: The first two equations show that both metrics H and \eta are indeed dynamical. Since schematically \Box_{\eta}H=\partial_{X}\partial_{P}H , the last equation essentially says that the phase space metric can depend only on X or only on P . In the first case, we recover the usual graviton mode propagation on this space-time.
where: §2.2 Two scale Renormalization Group, after eq. (2)
reading: These are linearized background equations from a fixed point of a double RG. They restrict H to depend on X only or on P only: the field equations confine it to one section but do not say which. Only the X case is developed. The record has this (notes/toy-lagrangian.md: 'solved along either null line').

quote: In ordinary quantum mechanics we may, depending on convenience, choose a position or momentum basis of states; it is a fundamental property of quantum theory that this choice of polarization is immaterial. In quantum gravity, if all probes agree on what we mean by space-time, then we have broken Born duality — there is a preferred choice of polarization, the space-time one.
reading: This is the passage #11 §3 quotes, and it is on p. 3 as cited. The preferred polarization comes from agreement among probes (absolute locality), not from a vacuum.

quote: In the absence of interactions amongst strings, it is perhaps not obvious that different strings should view the same Lagrangian submanifold as space-time.
reading: Without interactions each probe could pick its own Lagrangian. Here the choice is per probe, not per vacuum.

quote: Colloquially, it is only when probes talk to one another, through interactions, that they compare their choices.
reading: Agreement on a spacetime is made by interactions between probes (relative locality). No mechanism or vacuum is given.

quote: In the context of the metastring, the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric \eta
reading: FLM put the rigidity of quantum theory in a flat η, and they mean to relax it. P2′ puts rigidity in ω ('symplectic rigidity ≡ constancy of ℏ') and makes η emergent. Both make η non-rigid, but they disagree on what stays rigid.

quote: However, the Born proposal is not enough. As we have pointed out in [3], in the metastring theory we must take \eta to be dynamical as well. As we have seen above, it is \eta that governs the splitting of phase space into space and momentum space.
where: §2.1 More General Backgrounds and Born Geometries, p. 11
reading: η governs the splitting, and in [26S] itself it must be dynamical.

quote: It is relative locality that suggests that both \eta and H be dynamical. In particular, in canonical quantum theory H is a purely kinematical structure and \eta , which describes the choice of polarization, can be modified by unitary dynamics. Conversely, in the context of gravitational dynamics, \eta is a purely kinematical structure (because space-time provides the preferred basis or polarization), while H , through its space-time part, can be made dynamical.
reading: η 'describes the choice of polarization'. It is kinematical only in GR.

quote: When we introduce quantum theory into gravity, we have to make the neutral metric \eta dynamical, and thus in the context of quantum gravity, both H and \eta have to be dynamical.
reading: The paper #11 cites for the 'kinematical' attribution makes the polarization metric dynamical in quantum gravity. #11 P2′ credits this, which #11 §3's 'They treat the breaking as kinematical' does not reflect.

quote: not only the constant Q-metric H^{0} is promoted to an arbitrarily curved metric H , but also the P-metric and symplectic structure are allowed to be dynamical.
where: §2.3 Usual string viewed from phase space
reading: In the metastring ω is dynamical as well as η and H (eq. 41 calls all three 'dynamical'). P2′ keeps ω rigid, so the school's dynamical η comes in a setting that P2′ excludes.

quote: This generalization is one of the most interesting and will need to be dynamically constrained in order to give admissible backgrounds. In particular, it implies considering the new possibility where \eta is no longer a flat metric. This entails relaxing the condition that the splitting between space-time and energy-momentum is universal.
reading: A curved η means the splitting is no longer universal. The constraints are to come from dynamics and are not given.

quote: By keeping the property of maximal degeneracy, we keep the concept of a preferred Lagrangian defined by the metastring fields.
reading: The preferred Lagrangian is ker(η+ω), a property of the background fields of the sigma model. It is defined, not selected.

quote: In that respect it is interesting to note that the condition of absolute locality follows from the demand of worldsheet locality of observables.
reading: A consistency condition, worldsheet locality, leads to a single spacetime for all fields, the L-projectability condition. This is a kinematical selection, as #11 §3 says, though it confines fields to one section without saying which.

quote: What is new about this viewpoint is that it allows us to think about the choice of space-time inside phase space as a dynamical question.
where: §7 Quantum Lagrangians and Modular Space-time, p. 47 (v1 PDF)
reading: This is the phrase #11 §3 quotes. It is on p. 47, not p. 3, and #11 gives no page for it. The words are 'the choice of space-time inside phase space', not 'the breaking'.

quote: What is conceptually remarkable here is that this target space locality condition is selected by demanding worldsheet locality.
reading: The selector actually exhibited in this paper is a consistency requirement (worldsheet locality), not an energetic or vacuum mechanism.

quote: Allowing the notion of space-time to be dynamical goes hand in hand with allowing the \eta metric to become dynamical. In the metastring formulation new CFT deformation modes are allowed, including the winding modes, whose collective excitations correspond to deformations of the \eta background.
reading: η has field excitations: winding-mode collective excitations deform it. This is the nearest thing in the paper to η as a field with its own modes. No potential or vacuum analysis is given.

quote: Also, in this formulation T-duality exchanges the Lagrangian sub-manifold with its orthogonal complement.
reading: The other choice is the T-dual one, related by a symmetry of string theory and so equally lawful.

quote: it may offer new insights into standard problems in string theory, such as vacuum selection.
reading: This is the only use of 'vacuum selection': a hope about the string-vacuum problem, not about the polarization. The paper has no 'spontaneous', 'order parameter' or 'Goldstone' (0 hits).

quote: The paradox is resolved by recognizing that an observer’s notion of space corresponds to a choice of basis (a choice of polarization), and such a notion is acted upon by rotations. However, precisely because the underlying algebra is non-commutative, any such choice is unitarily equivalent to any other, and thus the action of rotations induces a superposition of modular spaces.
reading: A polarization is the observer's choice of basis, and every choice is unitarily equivalent to every other. In this paper the polarization is not a physical vacuum choice.

quote: The basic definition that we propose for a quantum space is that it is a choice of polarization for the representation of the Heisenberg algebra.
reading: Space is defined as a choice of polarization. The paper does not say what makes the choice.

quote: As a summary, we have seen that the choice of modular quantization \alpha_{\eta} is associated with the choice of a polarization metric \eta which determines a bilagrangian lattice (\Lambda,\eta) , also called Narain lattices.
reading: η enters as a parameter of the quantization, a choice, not as a field with a vacuum value.

quote: This is indeed the most natural choice and it shows that we cannot fully disentangle the kinematics (i.e., the definition of translation generators) from the dynamics.
reading: The modular vacuum is defined as the ground state of an 'energy' E_H = H^{AB}P_A P_B, so it depends on a chosen H. FLM say this mixes kinematics with dynamics.
